name: SCIE Buddhism Club
description: SCIE Buddhist Wisdom Club introduces classical Buddhist ideas in a simple and open way. Members study compassion, karma, anger, meditation, and emptiness through selected texts and school-life examples. Teachers and students can ask questions and join respectful discussions. People of all beliefs are welcome; no religious commitment is required.

name: ACA Together
description: A Cappella Club is a student-led vocal ensemble where members create music entirely through the human voice, without instrumental accompaniment. The club welcomes students with different levels of singing experience and provides a supportive environment for members to develop their vocal and performance skills. During weekly sessions, members will learn fundamental a cappella techniques, including vocal warm-ups, breathing, resonance, harmony, blending, rhythm, and ensemble listening. Members will be assigned suitable voice parts based on their vocal ranges and will work together to rehearse arrangements for school performances such as SGT and other events throughout the year. Beyond preparing for performances, the club aims to build a close and collaborative musical community. Through rehearsals, section practices, and performances, members will learn not only how to become more confident singers, but also how to listen, communicate, and contribute effectively as part of an ensemble.

name: AI Ethics & Governance Roundtable
description: AI Ethics & Governance Roundtable is a source-based discussion and writing ECA for students interested in how artificial intelligence should be developed, regulated and used. Each meeting examines a concrete policy question through primary materials such as legislation, regulatory guidance, institutional frameworks, research papers and real cases. Topics may include risk-based AI regulation, transparency and labelling of AI-generated content, copyright and training data, algorithmic bias, biometric surveillance, education, open-source models, frontier-model safety and responsibility for automated decisions. Members will distinguish facts, legal requirements, ethical principles and stakeholder interests before joining a moderated roundtable. They will then write short position memos that state a claim, address counterarguments and propose an actionable policy. No prior legal or technical knowledge is required. The aim is not to reach one approved opinion, but to develop evidence-based judgment, careful disagreement and responsible public reasoning. By the end of the semester, members will produce a reviewed collection of position papers and present selected arguments in a public AI governance forum.

name: Acupuncture & TCM
description: Our aim is to provide information about acupuncture and traditional Chinese medicines to students who are interested. We also teach the students how to diagnose and how to treat every-day injuries using a unique traditional Chinese method. Further more, we also do service learning by using our knowledge to benefit our community family, friends and social groups.

name: Aerodynamicists
description: The Aerodynamics Club is for students interested in understanding how air flows around objects and how these principles are applied in engineering. This semester, the club will introduce key topics such as fluid properties, pressure, viscosity, boundary layers, lift, drag, flow separation, and airfoil design. Sessions will combine short explanations with demonstrations, discussions, and practical activities so that members can connect physical theory with real aerodynamic applications. As the semester progresses, students will also be introduced to computational fluid dynamics (CFD), learning how computer simulations can be used to visualise and analyse airflow. Depending on members’ experience and interest, we will explore software such as OpenFOAM and PyFR and conduct simple aerodynamic modelling projects. No previous knowledge of aerodynamics or coding is required. The club is designed to be accessible to beginners while also offering opportunities for more experienced students to explore advanced topics. Our goal is to develop members’ understanding of physics, engineering, numerical modelling, and real-world aerodynamic design.

name: Aerodynamics & Simulation Club
description: Ever wondered why a Formula 1 car sticks to the ground, how aircraft wings generate lift, or how engineers test a design before it is ever built? In this ECA, you will turn your own ideas into 3D models using Rhino, then bring them into STAR-CCM+ to see how air, fluids, heat and other physical forces interact with your designs. Instead of simply learning software, you will work like an engineer: design, simulate, analyze, improve, and test again. Projects may include aerodynamic cars, aircraft wings, drones, turbines, cooling systems, or even designs of your own choice. No previous experience with 3D modelling or simulation is required—we will start from the basics and gradually move toward more advanced projects. If you enjoy engineering, physics, design, cars, aviation, or simply want to see whether your ideas actually work in the real world, this ECA gives you a chance to explore engineering beyond the classroom.

name: Ai for math
description: We are going to explore interplay between artificial intelligence and mathematics. To be more specific, we will guide how to install Rethlas and how to use it. Then we will teach formalizing math in calculus to help them better understand this topic.

name: Animal Studies Society
description: The Animal Science and Welfare Club is a student-led club exploring animal biology, behaviour, health, and welfare. Through discussions, presentations, case studies, interactive activities, and research, members will learn about how animals function, behave, and interact with humans. The club also examines real-world issues such as responsible animal care, conservation, animal ethics, and the challenges faced by animals in different environments. Our aim is to combine scientific knowledge with empathy and encourage students to develop a deeper understanding of animals and our responsibilities towards them.

name: Anime Club
description: We are a vibrant community dedicated to sharing the joy of anime. Our club hosts weekly screenings and anime discussions to explore the diverse culture of Japanese animation. Whether you're a seasoned otaku or a curious newcomer, join us to embark on an exciting journey through the world of anime!

name: AnthroPulse
description: The AnthnoPulse Lab is an anthropology-focused club dedicated to uncovering the hidden meanings in everyday life. We treat our school and city as living field sites, investigating how objects, spaces, and routines reflect human behavior and social change. Unlike traditional academic clubs, we don’t just read about culture—we go out to observe it. Through systematic fieldwork, interviews, and creative documentation, we explore questions like: How do students personalize their dorm spaces? How do different generations use the same public park? What do market transactions reveal about community values? Each semester, members collaborate on a micro-ethnography project, producing field notes, interview excerpts, and visual responses. The AnthnoPulse club is a space for curious minds to develop observational rigor, cultural empathy, and a nuanced understanding of the diverse communities we inhabit.

name: Apeiron PhyX
description: We are a physics club that aims to teach students computational physics content in a more accessible way. Also, we will hold discussions between students and physics experts to help them understand cutting-edge knowledge. Lastly, we plan to partner with other ECAs to gather SCIE students who love math and science, and organize various activities.

name: Apex Racing
description: Starting and evolving from SCIE RC Racing Club last year, Apex Racing is a brand new and fully developed RC racing team, that not only focus on engineering and racing, but also teamwork, collaboration skills, and abilities to adapt to new tasks. We need more than tech geeks, finance and public media department needs much more members to join us and fight together. In the ECA we are going to form a real racing team, with its typical structure. Members will have hand-on experience of dealing with a racing season, from the start with preparations, to the end winning the grand prize. During practice, everyone will have the opportunity to drive the 1/10 Touring Car to perform tasks, achieve standard lap time, and learn from the ECA leader about all technical knowledge related to RC racing cars. These knowledges can also be used on real cars. Furthermore, all spendings and costs during the season will rely on sponsors, and thus members do not need to pay for any additional material costs. In collaboration with other ECAs, we will be studying for all ranges of information. Feel free to join and enjoy a wonderful journey with professional Remote controlled cars.

name: Arts and Sciences
description: Formerly Introduction to Architecture, we broaden the content and aim to dismantle the traditional barriers between STEM and the Arts. Inspired by the interdisciplinary mindset championed by top universities like Harvard and Cambridge, we create a platform where members explore the connection between diverse fields like art, science, history, and technology. We hold lectures, discussions and hands-on activities, displaying our members’ work through an exhibition. Our curriculum includes learning foundational modelling skills (Blender, Rhino) and engaging in themed interdisciplinary lectures and experiments. We provide a collaborative and 100% English environment where beginners can master modelling tools, exchange ideas, and broaden their horizons.

name: BG Lab
description: BG Lab is a student-led ECA that introduces members to a wide range of board game genres, mechanics, and design concepts through both gameplay and analysis. Members will have the opportunity to design and develop their own original board games from scratch, progressing from an initial idea to rules, prototypes, playtesting, and a finished product. In addition, BG Lab aims to connect members with experienced board game designers and visual artists, giving them insight into the professional board game industry and, where possible, opportunities to collaborate with professionals to further develop their own projects.

name: Bacamera Filmmaker Club
description: Bacamera Filmmaker Club focuses on nourishing SCIEr who desire to make their own films and SCIEr who would like to systematically learn about film theories and the filmmaking process. We are the first filmmaking club that covers everything from theoretical courses and film analysis to practical experience on set in SCIE.

name: Baseball New Wave
description: Baseball

name: Basketball Development Centre
description: Will provide students with proper and systematic trainning sessions to help them develop personal skills and team work skills. Foster possible players for the FOBISIA tournament.

name: BioBío
description: The Biobío club is a student-led extracurricular activity dedicated to exploring biology through hands-on activities, field observation, and interdisciplinary projects. Rather than focusing on lectures or examination preparation, the club aims to make biology engaging and relevant to everyday life. Activities will include campus biodiversity surveys, species identification, and investigations into the biology behind familiar experiences such as plant pigments, fragrances, food, and nutrition. By connecting ecology, environmental science, molecular biology, and nutrition, members will explore the diversity of biological sciences while developing their own interests. The club welcomes students with different levels of biological knowledge and encourages curiosity, collaboration, and independent exploration.

name: BioChem Experiment club
description: Do extended experiments in school lab. Our club may use chemistry lab room at floor 8.

name: BioChem Fever
description: BioChem Fever is a student-led club designed to ignite curiosity and creativity in the fields of biology and chemistry. Our activities combine hands-on experiments, scientific discussions, and problem-based projects to help members deepen their understanding of the natural sciences beyond the classroom. The club will cover molecular biology, biochemistry, and applications in biotechnology, giving students the opportunity to explore fascinating topics such as enzyme activity, synthetic biology, and environmental applications of biochemistry. By integrating practical experiments with theory, members will gain confidence in experimental design, data analysis, and scientific communication. BioChem Fever aims to be both educational and enjoyable, cultivating teamwork and inspiring future scientists.

name: Brew Isle
description: Brew Isle is a place where we, with enthusiasm in coffee, brew coffee, taste coffee and discuss about coffee. The main focus is on hand-brewed coffee and boutique coffee. We discuss topics including origins, varieties, process methods, brewing techniques and so on. Every member here is free to share their unique thought with others, while discovering new knowledge about coffee.

name: Bureau of Unexplained Affairs
description: This ECA is a civil‑paranormal‑phenomenon research society. We explore reported anomalous cases, including UFO sightings, cryptids such as the Loch Ness Monster, and historical supernatural folklore. Rather than confirming whether paranormal events are real, our core goal is to analyse these accounts from historical, psychological and sociological perspectives. We will study classic materials such as 《Soulstealers: The Chinese Sorcery Scare of 1768》, comparing mass panics in history with modern‑day viral supernatural rumours. Members practise critical‑thinking, source‑checking and group discussion. We evaluate eyewitness reports, media narratives and social‑psychological causes behind collective belief.

name: Business Teaching Club
description: The Business Teaching Club is the club that can offer members the opportunity to gain practical insights into theoretical business knowledge. Furthermore, they have the chance to express this valuable information by voluntarily teaching primary school students. Whether one is an experienced entrepreneur, an aspiring business leader, or a curious student, our club serves as a dynamic platform for expanding both their business acumen and their contributions to others' knowledge.

name: Business practice club
description: BPC runs the annual rose selling event in the school carnival. We also work with the Harvard BPC program and train our students to be ready for the competition

name: Cantonese linguistics
description: This student-led Cantonese Linguistics club focuses on the academic study of Cantonese, a vital regional language with unique phonetics, grammar and cultural value. As a native Cantonese speaker, I will lead members to explore its linguistic features, compare it with Mandarin and other Chinese dialects, discuss tone systems, vocabulary evolution and local cultural language phenomena.

name: Chamber Music
description: The is an ECA of students who have high level of skills in a string or woodwind instrument play classical music together. We are a group of students who are dedicated to letting people to appreciate the beauty of classical music through our well-rehearsed performances on stage, including the openings for MUN, TED x SCIE, and Art weeks. This is an opportunity to unleash our emotions during busy school days and feel connected through playing the epic pieces composed by brilliant mind in the past, especially the pieces in the Baroque period and Romantic period. We would be contributing to the school’s vibrancy and variety while advocating the spirit of classical music as our core values.

name: ChannelKay
description: Channoglkay aims to provide students in SCIE and beyond with insights into incividual experiences of SCIE seniors,focusing on their personal growth and thoughts. We also wan to help peers get use to life at SCE, putting together an Al incorporated system in which students can ask questions about life and academics at SCE.

name: Charity Bake Sale
description: Led by Joyce Jiao and Yifan Liu. We bake cookies and sell them during major school wide events as well as DEI events on the UN calendar and donate all profits to DEI initiatives. We accompany our bake sale with advocacy posters and online articles pertaining to DEI.

name: Cheer SCIE
description: Official SCIE Cheerleading club: We perform during sports day and varsity games.

name: Chemistry Curiosity Club
description: Our ECA aims to stimulate students' interest in Chemistry. We will introduce a wide range of topics, including inorganic, organic and physical Chemistry. The seniors will be delivering detailed knowledge about each topic every week, thus enriching our members' knowledge of the subject and enabling them a perceptive understanding of the world of Chemistry. Our lab session every semester will enhance members interest through a series of simple but eye-opening experiments, which will be under the guidance of our supervisor, thus also ensuring the safety of the safety of this process. We won ECA award in two consecutive years.

name: Chinese Debate Club
description: We aim to build a highly skilled Chinese debate team that proudly represents SCIE. We welcome all students who are interested in or already skilled in Chinese debating, and will select a core team through tryouts. Our goal is to carve out a space for SCIE on the Chinese debating stage, and we firmly believe that in the future, Chinese debate will become one of SCIE’s shining hallmarks.

name: Chinese Traditional Fitness & Meditation
description: Introduce students to traditional Chinese fitness and meditation through basic Baduanjin, Tai Chi, stretching, breathing and mindfulness exercises. No previous experience is required. Sessions will focus on movement, balance, flexibility, concentration and relaxation, while also exploring the cultural background of these traditional practices.

name: Chronoscience
description: Chronoscience is a history club which aims explore the intersection between history and technology. Rather than treating history simply as a collection of past events, the club examines how technologies have shaped human connection, migration, communication, conflict, and collective memory, as well as how digital tools can change the ways we research and present history.

name: Climbing ECA
description: Climbing activity at school climbing wall

name: CognitAble
description: Our ECA focuses on neurodiversity and cognitive accessibility in school environments. We will introduce the concept of "cognitive variations" that result from genetic differences, the environments in which people grow up, and differences in how people think, and then explore how these variations may influence students’ experiences in school. Then, we will explain and examine cognitive barriers, such as ADHD, dyslexia, and autism, that can arise from everyday learning materials, classroom environments, and communication methods. Each session will focus on a different aspect of neurodiversity or cognitive accessibility, such as attention, memory, reading, sensory processing, or executive function. The most important component of CogniAble ECA is to investigate practical ways to reduce them. The ECA aims to connect concepts from cognitive science with practical changes in the school environment, with a focus on making information and everyday school experiences more cognitively accessible.

name: Cognitive Aquarium
description: Cognitive Aquarium is an experiment-based cognitive science and behavioural science club that requires no prerequisite in psychology background. We will give an intro about what is cognitive science and specify its comprising blocks and components. Participants will ideally gain skills on reading, writing, interpreting and summarising research studies throughout hands-on experiment process. Each typical session will be a deep dive into a specific cognitive science concepts—e.g. memory, decision-making, attention, perception, etc— and usually includes 1. A short lecture/explanation 2. An activity (such as a game, a social interaction game, or other interactive tasks) 3. Replication of an classical or fun experiment (with participants trying to summarise the results) 4. A post-class assignment to read a relevant paper, discuss interesting ideas or "fun facts" gleaned from it, and log them in a shared document.

name: Compus ESG Lab
description: Our club is dedicated to imparting to students some basic concepts about ESG. Meanwhile, we will use specific company cases to help students understand and train them to apply the abstract notions in practice. Furthermore, each semester, our club will select one campus or community issue, such as an investigation into food waste in the school canteen, to publish a report. Additionally, it is essential to equip members with literacy in dissecting ESG reports and investigative skills, such as visualisation of data and scoring & rubric design. Overall, our club is created to educate students to have a mindset that includes environmental concerns, social welfare and justice in administration when they are making financial and economic decisions for sustainability.

name: Constellation Lab — Student Opportunity & Project Collaboration
description: Constellation Lab is an interdisciplinary academic ECA that connects students with competitions, research opportunities and collaborative projects across business, STEM, social sciences, writing and community impact. Members will discover and evaluate opportunities, organise reliable information, and form teams based on complementary skills, interests, availability and commitment. The ECA will also develop and test CoQuest, a WeChat Mini Program that provides a verified opportunity calendar and a safe, structured team-matching process. Members may contribute through research, programming, product design, writing, data organisation, communication or project leadership. No previous competition or technical experience is required. The ECA welcomes students who are curious, responsible and willing to turn ideas and opportunities into meaningful projects.

name: Cosmology Horizon
description: Our ECA is an astronomy outreach club that aims to make astronomy accessible, engaging, and relevant to students with different levels of scientific background. Through regular student-led sessions, we introduce topics ranging from neutron stars, stellar evolution, and auroras to asteroid defense, Mars exploration, and the future of human spaceflight. Rather than focusing on highly technical theory, our sessions emphasize clear explanations, visual materials, discussion, and curiosity-driven exploration. A distinctive part of our ECA is our astronomy photography program. We have access to remotely operated telescopes located at astronomical observatories in Ningxia and other regions of China. Members can apply for observing time and use these telescopes to capture astronomical objects under the guidance of the current and former club presidents. This gives students an opportunity to move beyond learning about astronomy and actually observe and photograph the universe themselves. We also organize an annual visit to the Shenzhen Astronomical Observatory, where members can experience professional astronomical facilities and learn about the daily work of astronomers.

name: D-Sign
description: D-sign club is a design club that aims to deliver free pro‑bono design for local community shops and small‑and‑micro‑sized businesses. It not only provides a pathway for art lovers, writers, filmmaker students to utilize their talents to benefit their community, but also greatly enriches their portfolios with real life design rooted in local stories.

name: DECODE THE WORLD
description: DECODE THE WORLD is an interdisciplinary and project-based ECA that explores how mathematics, data, computer science, and scientific thinking can be used to understand and solve real-world problems. Each year we decode a different domain by breaking complex problems into measurable components to find patterns in data and building computational solutions. This year's theme is DECODE SOUND, exploring the science and technology behind sound through signal processing, Fourier analysis, spectrograms, algorithms, and AI. At the end of every session there is a short technical lesson with a practical experiment or mini-build, allowing members to immediately apply what they learn. No prior coding (we will be doing vibe coding) or music experience is required. The goal to learn how to apply knowledge from different disciplines to problems beyond the classroom

name: Desktop intelligence
description: This ECA focus on students’ interest, introducing them to electrical technology and building a robot at final.

name: Dodgeball
description: The dodgeball club is an organization dedicated to promoting the sport of dodgeball among students at our school. Our club's activities include weekly practices where members can work on their throwing and catching skills, as well as strategy and teamwork. We organize intramural games and pick-up games, which allow members to play in a more casual setting. Additionally, the members of the dodgeball club will be able to participate in the once-in-a-year dodgeball house event, providing our members with the opportunity to showcase their abilities and test their mettle against other players. Overall, our goal is to provide a fun and inclusive environment for students to enjoy the game of dodgeball, while also helping them to improve their physical fitness and teamwork abilities.

name: Downbeats
description: This ECA is a school band that provides a creative and collaborative space for musicians of all skill levels. Our primary focus is on contemporary and popular music, exploring various genres from rock and pop to jazz and funk. We aim to develop our members' instrumental proficiency, stage presence, and ability to perform as a cohesive unit. We prepare for school events, concerts, and competitions, fostering a sense of community and shared passion for music. The band is a platform for members to express themselves musically, build confidence, and contribute to the school's vibrant cultural life.

name: Dragon's Den: TTRPG society
description: Dragon's Den is a platform for SCIE students interested in tabletop roleplaying games such as Dungeons and Dragons to meet new friends and form campaigns. The whole ECA is a network of creativity. Our members post and and exchange art of their characters, discuss theories about lore and worldbuilding, and unleash their inner creative spirits when they roleplay as their characters in our magical, medieval fantasy dungeon.

name: Dynamics of Stories and Mind
description: DSM is a club that intends to focus on the behavioural and developmental aspects of psychology. We aim to expand students' knowledge of various types of psychological experiments by incorporating literature and media into the lessons. The club seeks to explore the psychological theories and disorders reflected in literary and media characters, and explain the experiments done by past psychologists involved with the disorder (e.g Freud with Harry Potter dreams, or tie Pavlov to 1984 by George Orwell). At the end of every session, the club leader and members are encouraged to come up with a short story with characters sharing the same mental health problem. By the end of the semester, the club will compile the stories into a student-produced psychology magazine/journal, joining creative storytelling with rigorous academic insights.

name: E-girls
description: Our ECA is a K-pop dance performance group that aims to promote dance culture and provide students with opportunities to develop confidence, creativity, and teamwork through choreography and stage performances. The group will participate in school events such as Halloween activities and SCIE Got Talent Show

name: Earth Rangers
description: This is a geology club where students can explore the forces and processes that shape the Earth. Each secession begins with an intriguing earth mystery. Why do earthquakes and volcanoes occur in plate boundaries? How can seismic waves reveal Earth’s interior? Why are some mountains red? How do glaciers create fjords, and how can ocean temperatures affect weather around the world? We will first go through the basic knowledge of geology such as rock cycle and sedimentary processes. Then we will talk about interesting geographical phenomena and landscapes. Some topics and activities will be selected through member voting, allowing the club to reflect students’ interests. We will use maps, photographs, rock samples, models, real data and group challenges to examine evidence and develop explanations.

name: Earth Three-Body Organization
description: Earth Three-body Organization was founded in 2023. Inspired by the sci-fi "The Three-body Problem," this community was founded to gather enthusiasts of the book, given its widespread influence around the globe. After reforms, we held weekly seminars discussing the literary, scientific and humanitarian aspects of the novel. Everyone will have a nametag, and will be invited by the host to share their thoughts in the seminars. Such activity format was inspired by US liberal arts based education, valuing interdisciplinary, freedom of expression and belonging. Apart from weekly activities, ETO also held projects. In 2024, we attempted to invite the book's author, Mr. Cixin Liu, to give speech at SCIE, but received a kind rejection. Last year, we successfully invited the department head of Astronomy of Sun Yat-sen Univeristy, Prof. Jun Cui, to speak at SCIE, making tangible community impact. Next year, we will be focusing on publishing and creating an archive to the content of our discussion

name: Echo
description: This ECA combines introductory social‑psychological knowledge with light‑hearted recreational activities to promote accessible mental‑well‑being awareness among students. We deliver beginner‑friendly psychology tips covering emotion regulation, stress management and self‑acceptance, avoiding overly complex academic jargon. Most sessions prioritize entertaining interactive segments, including casual group discussions, mini games and scenario‑sharing, instead of rigid lectures. Members will learn practical, daily‑usable mental‑health skills to recognize personal emotional signals and build healthier mindsets. This activity creates a safe, relaxed peer space, where participants can reduce psychological pressure, understand simple social‑psychological logic, and support one another’s mental wellness in an enjoyable atmosphere.

name: Eduspark
description: EduSpark is a student-led education and social impact ECA that aims to make learning more engaging, accessible, and connected to the wider world. Members explore real-world topics such as culture, history, economics, technology, mathematics, sustainability, and global inequality, and transform what they learn into interactive educational activities. Rather than simply volunteering as tutors, members will work collaboratively to design discussion-based lessons, educational games, workshops, and outreach projects for younger students and communities with fewer opportunities to access diverse perspectives. The ECA is built around four principles: curiosity, critical thinking, global perspective, and student empowerment. Members will develop their own ideas, test activities, receive feedback, and improve them through reflection. Our work will include both on-campus educational activities and community outreach, including the EduSpark Shanxi teaching project. Through these experiences, we hope to create a sustainable cycle: students learn, students design, students teach, and students create positive social impact. Ultimately, EduSpark aims to help both our members and the students we reach see a bigger world, think more deeply, and believe that they can make a difference.

name: Electricity& Magnetism Society
description: This is a club that aims to provide introductory undergraduate level physics course for students interested in physics, especially electricity and magnetism. This course is specially designed with a blend of in depth physics with real life interactive demonstrations that allows students to observe learn physics in reality intuitively. We will be following the greats of the physcis history, building equipments from scratch: E.g battery out of copper coins and vinega, derive Gauss's law and use it to prove where charge sits on a conductor, and by the end of the course studnets will hopefully master three out of the four Maxwell Equations .No prior knowledge is assumed in this course(basic algebra understanding in needed, preknowledge to calculas may be helpful, but will be covered).

name: Electromagnetics & Optics Society
description: The Electromagnetics & Optics Society is a theory‑oriented club focused on the fundamental principles of electricity, magnetism, and light. Our sessions cover topics such as Ohm’s law, electric fields, potential energy, Lorentz force, magnetic flux, electromagnetic induction, Lenz’s law, motional and induced EMF, photoelectric effect, double‑slit interference, grating diffraction, and half‑wave loss. We meet weekly for guided discussions and problem‑solving sessions. The emphasis is on building a clear conceptual understanding and working through challenging questions together. Simple demonstrations may be included occasionally to help visualize abstract ideas, but the main focus remains on theoretical reasoning and group discussion. Members are encouraged to ask questions and share their thinking. All students with an interest in physics are welcome, regardless of prior background.

name: English Teaching Club
description: The English Teaching Club is a student-led service club dedicated to making English learning more accessible, engaging, and enjoyable for younger students. Through volunteer teaching, interactive activities, and educational outreach, club members create lessons tailored to students’ different learning needs and interests. Beyond teaching English, ETC aims to build meaningful connections between students and the wider community. Members develop lesson-planning, communication, leadership, and teamwork skills while encouraging younger learners to gain confidence in using English. Through regular classes, community outreach, and creative learning activities, the club strives to make language education more inclusive and empowering.

name: Entrepreneurship Club
description: The Entrepreneurship Club aims to introduce students to both the theoretical and practical sides of entrepreneurship. Inspired by my experience at LaunchX, where I studied entrepreneurial concepts and developed a startup with my team, I wanted to create a space at school for students who are interested in business but may not yet have opportunities to explore entrepreneurship in practice. Through interactive workshops, case discussions, and group projects, members learn how to identify market opportunities, conduct market research, develop value propositions and MVPs, understand basic business models and finance, and pitch ideas effectively. Rather than focusing only on lectures, the club encourages students to apply these concepts to real-world problems. For example, members have discussed developing a platform that connects food-delivery services while providing calorie information, personalized dietary planning, and restaurant recommendations for users with fitness goals. Ultimately, the club hopes to help students become more observant, creative, and analytical problem-solvers while gaining practical experience in turning an initial idea into a viable business concept.

name: Every Girl Can
description: Every Girl Can (EGC) is the largest girls’ football club at Shenzhen College of International Education (SCIE), providing a welcoming and supportive space for girls to develop their football skills and passion for the game. Whether you are an experienced player or have never played football before, EGC offers professional training designed to help every member fully develop her skills, build confidence, and enjoy the excitement of playing and competing. Beyond football, it is also a place to meet like-minded young female footballers, make new friends, and become part of a supportive community.

name: Fanart Club
description: Fanart Club is a place where students can make art and share their love for movies, books, games, and other fictional stories. We want to build a friendly space where people with similar interests can talk freely about their favorite characters and worlds. During ECA time, we work together to come up with simple and fun ideas for art, as well as give members prompts and suggestions to help them get started. Students don't need to be a great artist to join, any beginners are welcome too. The club is about having fun, being creative, and meeting new friends who like the same things you do. We also share tips and support each other.

name: Feminism Club
description: Feminism Club is a club that promotes gender equality ideals, sharing and communicating gender study theories with other students, and reading materials from different cultural backgrounds.

name: Fictional Engineering Club
description: Fictional Engineering offers weekly lectures and hands-on workshops covering Engineering Design, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, 3D Modelling, and 3D Printing & Rapid Prototyping. Our project-based approach takes students from fundamental engineering concepts and tool usage to designing, prototyping, and building complete projects.

name: Figure Skating Club
description: The Figure Skating Club is a student-led ECA for students interested in figure skating and sports health. During weekly sessions, members will learn about skating techniques, sports rehabilitation, injury prevention, recovery, and mobility. Once or twice each semester, members who are available will have the opportunity to go ice skating together. The club aims to combine the enjoyment of skating with practical knowledge about staying healthy and active in sports.

name: Flawesome Museum Club
description: This ECA uses art and storytelling to explore the imperfections, challenges, and unexpected moments that shape people’s lives. This year, its main focus will be elderly care and the experiences of older adults, using creative expression to encourage students to look beyond stereotypes of aging and understand the people behind them. Students will visit elderly-care communities and related facilities, where they will observe daily life, conduct interviews, and explore topics such as aging, memories, family relationships, loneliness, independence, dignity, and the changing relationship between generations. They will work together to create a documentary that records these experiences and gives elderly participants an opportunity to share their own stories and perspectives. Alongside documentary filmmaking, students will transform what they learn into different forms of art, including photography, painting, writing, illustration, and installation. These works will explore themes such as memory, aging, vulnerability, resilience, and human connection. The creative process will encourage students to reflect on their own assumptions about aging while developing empathy, communication, and storytelling skills. The ECA will culminate in an exhibition combining student artwork, documentary footage, photographs, and other materials collected throughout the project. By bringing these stories to a wider audience, the exhibition will encourage conversations about elderly care and intergenerational understanding, ultimately turning individual stories and everyday experiences into meaningful narratives of connection.

name: Forensic Science Club
description: This club provides a platform for students who are interested in forensic science and forensic pathology to share their knowledge. The club bridges classroom theory with real-world forensic practice, fostering both expertise and passion for solving complex cases, in form of lecture and discussion sessions.

name: Formula One Club
description: I want to construct a community in the SCIE about the Formula 1. I want to offer a place for fans in the campus to communicate with each other and share their understanding as well as their enthusiasm towards the sport.

name: French Film
description: The French Film ECA is a space for students to watch and discuss a wide range of French-language films together. Through films from different genres, periods, and French-speaking regions, members will explore French culture, society, history, and cinematic aesthetics. After each film, members will be encouraged to share their personal views and interpretations in a friendly and open discussion. We believe that listening to different opinions can help us notice details and perspectives that we may have missed on our own. Through these discussions, we hope to develop a deeper appreciation of cinema and a more thoughtful way of viewing the world. The ECA welcomes everyone, regardless of their level of French or previous knowledge of film. English subtitles will be provided when necessary. Our main aim is to enjoy French-language cinema together while learning from the films and from one another.

name: FunTrade
description: FunTrade is a friendly ECA for beginners that aims to awake students’ awareness and interest in finance. By introducing basic financial concepts, investment knowledge and real-world financial events, the club helps students develop financial thinking and understand how finance connects with everyday life.

name: Fundamental Physics Club
description: The Theoretical Physics Club is a student-led academic ECA designed to introduce students to fundamental physics that can help consolidate their background knowledge. We will not delve into very complicated topics, and members are only required to know P1 Calculus. Using Physics for Scientists and Engineers (6th Edition) by Paul A. Tipler and Gene Mosca as our main textbook, we explore fundamental concepts through a combination of guided teaching, mathematical derivations, conceptual discussions, and challenging problem-solving. The club will cover major areas of physics including mechanics, oscillations and waves, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, optics, and introductory modern physics. Sessions will be interactive, where members are encouraged to discuss and challenge each other with their own understandings. It will operate more likely as a study group rather than lecture-based classes.

name: Gastronomie
description: This ECA is an interdisciplinary club integrating food history, food politics, cultural anthropology and practical culinary techniques. It moves beyond casual food‑tasting activities. Members explore how ingredients travelled across empires, how food reflects power structures, social stratification and global trade. We also cover classical cooking fundamentals alongside avant‑garde modernist cuisine including molecular gastronomy.

name: Geographical Society
description: Some extended and advanced content on IGCSE geography and homemade case studies, helping students to broaden their knowledge and revise their classwork on geography. Part of the contents may be given according to AS, AP or AL geography. Non-geography students can also learn about geography in the ECA. Sometimes games can be held for students to learn geography. In addition, sometimes quiz games about geography will be held during our ECA class.

name: GirlUp SCIE
description: Girl Up is a student-led club dedicated to promoting gender equality and creating a space for students to learn, discuss, and take action on issues affecting girls and women. Through discussions during club session, volunteering work with non-profit communities and yearly summits, we hope to turn awareness into meaningful action. Whether you are passionate about gender equality or simply curious to learn more, Girl Up is a place to share your voice, hear different perspectives, and make a difference within and beyond our school community.

name: Girls Basketball Club
description: Plan to organize basketball training every Monday afternoon for girls who would like to learn and play basketball. Leading by PE teachers, this club is also aiming to train and prepare for the upcoming tryout of the school varsity team. Giving every students in SCIE an opportunity to enjoy playing basketball, the club has already have more than 3 years of history and has proficient experiences.

name: Glow & Grow
description: Glow & Grow is a student-led club that fosters confidence, wellness, and creativity within the school community. The teenage years are often marked by self-doubt, insecurities, and pressure from societal standards. Our club provides a safe and uplifting environment where students can strengthen their psychological resilience, developing a healthier relationship with themselves and others, and also providing professional guidance to enhance self-care skills, therefore enhancing confidence. Through activities in confidence-building, journaling, self-expression and stress management, our eca “Glow & Grow” aims to spread positivity throughout the school’s atmosphere. By helping members feel comfortable in their own appearance and encouraging self-acceptance, the club contributes to a more supportive, empathetic, and confident student body. The ultimate goal is not only personal growth for members, but also the creation of a school-wide culture of encouragement, self-belief, and community care.

name: Great Books Society
description: Great Books Society is a student-led reading and discussion club for students interested in philosophy, literature, history, politics, and the fundamental questions of human life. Each week, members will read a short text or selected excerpts from an influential work and discuss a central question raised by it: What is justice? What makes a good life? Are we truly free? What do we owe to others? What makes political authority legitimate? Possible readings will include works by Plato, Aristotle, Confucius, Shakespeare, John Stuart Mill, Nietzsche, Hannah Arendt, and other major thinkers and writers from different intellectual traditions. No previous knowledge of philosophy is required, and readings will be kept manageable and accessible. Meetings will combine close reading, guided discussion, short debates, thought experiments, and student-led presentations. Rather than looking for one “correct” interpretation, members will learn to question assumptions, examine arguments, listen carefully to different perspectives, and develop their own reasoned responses to enduring human questions.

name: GreenRoot Society
description: GreenRoot Society is a student-led community dedicated to exploring the connections between environmental change and human health—starting with soil. Our journey begins with personal story from Fujian, where agricultural pollution have harmed local farmland, showing the hidden urgency of soil protection. Members will then participate in the Out of Eden Learn – Introduction to Planetary Health learning journey, inspired by Paul Salopek’s slow journalism walk around the world. Through four “Footsteps,” we will: 1. Observe – Take mindful walks in our communities to notice and record environmental and health-related changes. 2. Connect – Build concept maps linking environmental changes such as pollution or biodiversity loss with specific human health impacts. 3. Investigate – Focus on one planetary health issue, research it through observation, interviews, and reliable resources, and share findings. 4. Act – Identify daily choices that affect planetary health and create advocacy resources to inspire change. Through GreenRoot Society, students will combine observation, scientific thinking, and storytelling to become thoughtful, informed advocates for the planet—proving that local actions can contribute to global health.

name: HEART BEAT
description: Our club is open to students from all disciplines who have an interest in understanding human personality psychology. We welcome anyone eager to explore the intricacies of psychology and introduce our club members to a wide range of professional knowledge on psychology, including Typology, personality psychology, analytical psychology and psychodynamic. Our club members are able to enjoy activities including lectures and workshops, as ECA leaders will share their research and insights on various topics related to psychology. Besides, they can also join volunteering projects that helps in explore psychology more in actions. Members can discuss theories with practical examples in reality to gain a better understanding. Our original objectives are to build a comprehensive understanding of psychology and to create an interactive environment where members can discuss and explore various aspects of psychology. Moreover, we also aim to help members gain a deeper understanding of their own personalities and foster personal growth. Join our club to delve into the fascinating world of personality psychology, connect with passionate peers, and listen to the heartbeat from every personality type.

name: HELPHANT
description: HELPHANT is a student-led organization dedicated to raising awareness of elephant conservation, and broader environmental issues and animal welfare through education, art, and public engagement. Through social media campaigns, educational activities, and charity sales, we aim to help more people understand the challenges facing elephants and encourage meaningful action to support international conservation efforts. Beyond animal protection, HELPHANT also seeks to make community service more inclusive by creating opportunities for people from different backgrounds to participate, express themselves, and contribute to society. We believe that small actions can connect people and create lasting impact.

name: Heartbreak Vaccine Club
description: The Heartbreak Vaccine Club is a student organization dedicated to promoting mental health and well-being on campus. Through peer mentoring, we provide a safe, supportive, and non-judgmental space where students can share their struggles with academics, relationships, and everyday life. Our members are trained in basic counseling and active listening skills, fostering empathy and understanding. Beyond one-on-one support, we also run a public platform to share accessible psychology knowledge and practical strategies for emotional resilience. Our mission is to normalize conversations around mental health and to build a campus culture of care, empathy, and connection.

name: Helping Unique Growing Souls
description: HugS(Helping Unique Growing Souls) is determined to provide help for the children with physical disabilities by multiple methods, for example, advocacy, education, and hands-on volunteer activities. Children with disabilities include those with physical disabilities, intellectual or cognitive disorders, and neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism spectrum disorder. Although awareness of providing special education to those children has improved in recent years, the phenomenon of a lack of public understanding, social stigma, and limited opportunities for accessing inclusive education persists. As a result, the primary aim of our club would be to improve their situation in society in the long term and provide common knowledge of them to those with limited understanding. By collaborating with local welfare centers, we want to provide more meaningful social engagement for students and the community so that they are able to engage with these special children and understand their special situation and lived experiences. Members are also encouraged to participate in awareness campaigns and the promotion of special education.

name: Hermanity
description: Humanities and Female Lens are two key words for this ECA. Humanities play a crucial role in our lives, especially in the world we now live in. Without literature, history, or philosophy, STEM would become lifeless numbers. Therefore, recognizing the importance of the humanities and how it influences our world is essential for personal and societal growth. In order to understand humanities, we have to approach it with different perspectives. Although there are several ECAs that focus on humanities, this ECA stands out as unique because it offers knowledge through a new, female perspective. Due to gender inequality, many influential women have been overlooked, and their contributions often went unrecognised. ‘Hermanity’ aims to help students appreciate the value of the humanities through a female lens and foster students’ critical thinking, collaboration, and public speaking skills. We thrive to reverse the stereotypes linked with humanities and overcome difficulties in reading and writing. Overall, we aim to foster student’s intrinsic motivations by giving members the opportunities to learn, and offer them a new lens when viewing our world.

name: ISL BOYS VOLLEYBALL
description: ECA for ISL Boys team

name: ISL GIRLS VOLLEYBALL
description: ECA for the School Volleyball team

name: Integrated Strategies Strategies Integrated
description: Integrated Strategies Strategies Integrated is an ECA that explores how history can be learned, represented and debated through video games, board games and strategy games. Members will look at how games set in different periods, such as Ancient Rome, medieval kingdoms, the World Wars or the Cold War, present historical events, leaders, societies and conflicts. We will discuss what games get right, what they simplify, and how game design influences our understanding of the past. Students will also try short challenges such as analysing historical accuracy, comparing games with real sources, and designing their own mini history game concepts. This ECA combines academic discussion with interactive activities, making history more engaging and memorable. It is suitable for students who enjoy history, gaming, storytelling, strategy and critical thinking.

name: InvestNow
description: InvestNow aims to make finance accessible, practical, and intellectually engaging, especially for students with little or no prior experience. Through interactive lessons, real-world cases, portfolio simulations, and discussions of current financial news, members will gradually develop the ability to understand businesses, interpret basic financial information, evaluate risk and return, and form their own investment opinions. The semester will culminate in a stock pitch, where students apply what they have learned to research, analyze, and defend an investment idea. Following feedback from previous members, we have redesigned our curriculum to provide a much stronger foundation before introducing advanced material. In addition, our experienced academic team, with strong results in national and international economics and investment competitions, also offers optional advanced sessions covering topics such as DCF valuation, portfolio and risk modelling, and derivatives. Beyond weekly teaching, InvestNow has already developed into a wider platform for financial education and student collaboration. We have organized two inter-school investment competitions involving students from schools spanning Suzhou to Shenzhen, collaborated with the Global Citizenship team to present social-enterprise projects during Sustainability Week, and have been invited to serve as one of the organizing societies for a seven-school Greater Bay Area investment competition.

name: IoT Business Simulator
description: We are a student-led club where technology meets entrepreneurship. Members from engineering, business, design, and other backgrounds work together to turn real-world problems into IoT products using ESP32 and other accessible technologies. From identifying a problem and conducting market research to designing, prototyping, testing, and marketing a product on real world platforms, members experience the complete journey from idea to product. In addition, we design activities that directly focus on benefiting your US application, blending ideas of leadership, creativity, and social impacts.

name: JGG
description: JGG is a music club built on joy, energy, and good vibes. The name comes from the Chinese “Jiao Gao Gao,” meaning “standing on tiptoes and reaching higher.” It also stands for “Just Get Groovy.” We are a group of music lovers who enjoy playing, creating, and jamming together. Our style blends rock, pop, and indie influences. We rehearse regularly, write original songs, and perform at campus and city events. We believe making music should be fun, not stressful. Whether you play an instrument or just love to sing and listen, everyone is welcome. Join JGG, get groovy, and turn the volume up!

name: JUNE East Asian Dialogue
description: Our club focus on the contemporary and traditional cultural expressions across East Asia, especially on literature, comics, visual storytelling, fan culture, and other forms of popular media. Through close reading and cross-cultural discussion, members will examine how cultural works reflect the cultural environments in which they are created. The club aims to explore the broader ideas and social changes embedded within them, while also considering similarities and differences across different regions and cultural contexts.

name: Latino Dance Club
description: The Latino Dance Club aims to gather students passionate about or interested in Latin dance. We will meet weekly to practice moves, learn choreography, and prepare performances for school events. Members will train in a variety of Latin dance styles, including Cha-cha, Rumba, Samba, Paso doble and Jive. This club seeks to foster teamwork, confidence, and a love for dance among members. Whether refining technique by diving deeper into Latin rhythm and movement or discovering a new hobby，members will thrive in an inclusive, lively, and ‘Latino’ environment.

name: Lego World Monuments
description: LEGO World Monuments is a creative, hands-on after-school club where students explore famous landmarks and monuments from around the world and recreate them using LEGO bricks. The club is ideal for students who enjoy LEGO, building, architecture, travel, history and discovering fascinating places around the world. They HAVE to complete this Cathédrale Notre-Dame de Paris LEGO thing before the end of my days!!!!!!!!!

name: Life Pawnshop
description: Life Pawnshop is an ECA focusing on scientific self-exploration through cognitive psychology and community building. Instead of relying on superficial and changeable personality tests such as MBTI, this club uses psychological theories, cognitive bias experiments, value-choice games and movie analysis to help students identify what combination of personality traits makes them who they are, inner goals they might not have recognized yet, and subconscious preferences. I hope to create a safe space for students to “drop the mask”, see their true selves, and learn to build a psychological defense system against external stressors. At Life Pawnshop, we will try to be honest, even if that means we are unsure, confused, and even awkward. But we will walk out braver and more confident.

name: Life-Health Club
description: There is no prior competition experience is required—students in grades 9–11 who are passionate about biology, public health, or social service are all welcome! We prioritize hands-on practice over lectures, applying classroom knowledge to real-world problems—focusing on aging populations, home environmental hygiene, mental and physical health among seniors, child left-behind health, and youth public health. You’ll experience the full project lifecycle: from research design and fieldwork to community education. You’ll build authentic, application-ready materials, portfolios, and research outcomes for U.S. college admissions. The club offers diverse roles that support academic profiles—whether you excel at lab work, writing, interviews, or data analysis, there’s a place for you.

name: Luminara Detectives Club
description: This is a platform for all detective fans in SCIE.Here you can learn detective knowledge that you might ever know, we provide lectures about detective culture and criminology (such as Criminal Psychology Lesson and Detective culture history).However the club is more about interest rather than theorist things! We play logic-reasoning games and hold Detective novel discussion regularly.Sometimes we watch detective movies together. Moreover we will plan some activity face to whole school like the detective game that we did last year on Halloween Night.

name: Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence Club (MLxAI)
description: SCIE ML×AI is a hands-on AI and data science ECA open to students with or without prior machine-learning experience. It develops members through three connected areas: Data Science, using Kaggle competitions to learn data analysis, validation, modelling and submission; AI Olympiads, using NOAI/IOAI-style problems to build deep-learning intuition and problem-solving insight; and Agentic Engineering, using prompts(a.k.a Agentic Skills), coding agents and multi-agent systems to implement AI models efficiently. No prior experience with coding is required as members will not copy code line by line. AI tools handle much of the implementation, while students define tasks, run experiments, evaluate results and decide how to improve their models. Seven guided sessions establish shared foundations in agent setup, tabular modelling, NLP, computer vision, Transformers and multimodal learning. The ECA then continues as a collaborative problem-solving lab using real datasets and competition tasks. Members may work independently or in teams, prepare competition submissions and present their methods, results and lessons to the school community.

name: Magicians' Awake in SCIE
description: Seen magic on the streets and wondered how they did it? Wanted to learn magic but never had a chance? Don't know how to practise magic? Join Magicians' Awake in SCIE now and experience the full-on magic tutorial! From simple card tricks to advanced mind manipulation, we've got it all!

name: Mania Aviators
description: Mania Aviators aim to provide a platform in SCIE for discussions about aviation, promoting this small industry by revealing the secretes beneath. The group of specialists in the ECA gives lectures to members which cover all major careers in the industry, exploring possible personalised career paths for members at the same time. Nonetheless, the ECA also welcomes members to teach classes regarding fields of their interest.

name: Math & Computer Science Club
description: Math & Computer Science Club focuses on algorithms, programming, and mathematical thinking beyond the school curriculum. Members will explore classic algorithms, data structures, computational problems, and their mathematical foundations through explanations, coding, and group discussion. The club is open to students with different levels of programming experience.

name: Math Odyssey
description: Math Odyssey focus on math competition tutoring and discussion. Our ECA is devoted to creating a professional and adaptable environment for students who are interested in math and not satified by the school curriculum and students who potentially want to apply math-related major in future. We will systematically teach topics in math contests. Our weekly course introduces Algebra, Combination, Geometry etc and past paper questions from contests. We will focus on some mainstream contests like AMC, AIME, BMO and occasionally included some advanced maths topics such as abstract algebra, and almost anything you want to learn about maths! Except for the weekly lessons, the club will also provide a platform for members to discuss intriguing problems, share creative solutions and find like-minded peers.

name: Math and Engineering Teaching Club
description: Math and Engineering Teaching Club intend to deliver high-quality lessons in various subjects such as math, chemistry, physics, computer science and economics to primary school students from school such as Green Oasis School. We will pre-prepare concise teaching syllabus and power point according to the interest of our members and the intention of students. Each week, we will go teaching offline, conduct creative acticities and record our teaching/learning outcome through various ways such as poster, student presentation, debate and etc.

name: Math-Physics Exploration
description: Physics–Math Exploration is a student-led academic club for students who would like to explore how mathematical ideas become tools for understanding physical systems. Starting from familiar classroom topics such as motion, forces, waves and energy, each session will begin with a modelling question(near our learning curriculum): What should we represent? Which assumptions are reasonable? What can the mathematics predict, and where does the model stop working? Sessions will combine short explanations(trying with both languages), guided discussion, and one or two carefully chosen problems(for each session). Useful mathematical tools—including vectors, trigonometry, parameterisation, graphs, introductory calculus ideas and data analysis—will be introduced when they become useful, rather than as isolated techniques. The aim is not simply to move ahead through a syllabus, but to develop curiosity, precise reasoning and confidence in turning everyday questions into solvable physical models. Students with different levels of mathematical experience are welcome; optional extension problems and small projects will provide further challenge.

name: Mathematical Modeling Club
description: As one of the biggest ECA on campus, this club is dedicated to preparing students for the High School Mathematical Contest in Modeling (HiMCM) by COMAP, a globally recognized academic competition. Our mission is to equip members with advanced mathematical knowledge and skills, extending beyond the classroom, to solve complex real-world problems creatively. The club offers training in mathematical modeling, data analysis, and report writing, enhancing reasoning, teamwork, and innovation. Members will learn from past winners, work with experienced mentors( including alumni), and participate in simulated competitions, all aimed at excelling on an international stage. We actively participate in schools themed week and activities, and have won the "Most Creative ECA"(2/380+) in 24, and the “Most Popular ECA” in 25, with 2 teams of members won a M prize and 1 team won the F prize in HiMCM, one team won F prize in IMMC.

name: Mathematical Structures Society
description: Mathematical Structures Society (MSS) is a student-led mathematics exploration community that aims to help students discover the deeper ideas behind mathematics beyond the standard curriculum. Rather than focusing only on competition training or solving individual problems, MSS encourages students to explore how mathematical ideas are connected through patterns, structures, and logical reasoning. Through workshops, discussions, problem-solving sessions, and student presentations, members will gradually develop the ability to move from concrete problems toward abstract mathematical thinking. The club will introduce accessible topics from areas such as mathematical reasoning, combinatorics, number theory, symmetry, graph theory, cryptography, and introductory abstract algebra. By connecting mathematics with real-world applications, art, technology, and everyday phenomena, MSS hopes to make advanced mathematical thinking approachable for high school students.

name: Mathematical and Physical Society
description: Our society is a student-run academic group focused on mathematics and physics, operating within our school. The core activity is simple: we invite experienced members—senior students who have a solid grasp of particular topics—to give regular walk-through sessions on standard textbooks, helping fellow students navigate difficult derivations, solve problems step by step, and clarify common misconceptions. Unlike formal lectures, our sessions are interactive and discussion-friendly; attendees are encouraged to interrupt with questions whenever something is unclear. We believe that peer-to-peer explanation, coming from someone who recently struggled with the same material, is often the most accessible bridge between a dense textbook and genuine understanding. Beyond our weekly sessions, we maintain a small public account where we share concise reading notes, worked examples, and occasional popular-science pieces. We might also collaborate with the school's sci-fi club on informal joint meetups in the future, where we pick a scientific idea from a novel or film and walk through how plausible it really is under known physics—just for fun and curiosity. Our society is not about grand ambitions; it is about building a friendly, low-pressure space where students who enjoy math and physics can share what they know, help each other learn, and maybe discover that these two subjects are less intimidating when tackled together.

name: Mathematics Beyond Problems
description: This is a student-led mathematics ECA focused on understanding mathematics beyond simply applying formulas to solve problems. The main focus will be on Further Mathematics and AS/AL Mathematics, with sessions exploring where mathematical concepts and formulas come from, why they work, and how different ideas are connected. Topics may also be selected according to members’ interests. Sessions will generally include teaching, discussion, problem solving, and mathematical exploration. Active members will also be encouraged to prepare and lead sessions on topics they are interested in.

name: Medlink
description: We are a biomedical extracurricular ECA for exploring the profound intersection of clinical science, ethics, and humanistic care. We delve deeply into common-seen medical cases, from stroke rehabilitation to euthanasia by first grounding each topic in its biological fundamentals. Our top mission is to understand the full spectrum of medicine—from cells to the bedside—while considering its ethical dimensions, and to practice with compassion. Every member collaborates to create in-depth articles and videos that will be posted on our official platforms to raise public awareness and funds for disability charities. Beyond theory, we bridge learning to practice through hospital and hospice shadowing.

name: MindBridge
description: MindBridge is a peer-driven forum for students passionate about mental health and clinical science. We explore core topics including psychopathology, evidence-based interventions, diagnostic systems, ethics, and the scientist‑practitioner model. Through interactive case discussions, journal article reviews, role‑play demonstrations, and occasional guest speakers, members gain a realistic preview of clinical psychology training and practice. Our sessions foster critical thinking, cultural humility, and the integration of research with real‑world clinical work. We aim to build a supportive community where curiosity about human behaviour meets rigorous scientific inquiry, helping members prepare for further study or careers in mental health. The ECA values diversity, empathy, and evidence‑based approaches, while also encouraging self‑reflection and personal growth. We welcome anyone interested in understanding psychological distress and healing, regardless of prior background, and we strive to reduce stigma around mental health through open, respectful dialogue.

name: Mindful Maker Club
description: Students will create handmade accessories and use the mandala as a base to create ornaments. We will explore creativity, focus, and self-expression through the art of mandala design. Using drawing, colouring, painting and recycled materials, we will create unique mandala artworks while developing collaborative skills and artistic confidence.

name: Model United Nations (MUN)
description: Model United Nations (MUN) at SCIE offers students an engaging platform to explore global affairs, diplomacy, and international relations. Designed as an academic and lecture-based ECA, weekly sessions provide structured guidance on geopolitics, parliamentary procedure inspired by the United Nations, resolution drafting, and effective public speaking. Members gain a comprehensive understanding of how international bodies operate while analyzing real-world global challenges. In addition to weekly instructional sessions, members have the opportunity to represent our school at external MUN conferences, applying their skills in competitive, multi-school debates. Furthermore, club members actively participate in organizing, planning, and hosting our school's annual MUN conference—a major event that fosters leadership, logistics management, and teamwork. Whether you are a beginner looking to build confidence or an experienced delegate aiming to refine your diplomatic skills, this ECA equips you with critical thinking and leadership abilities for the future.

name: Mosaic DIY
description: The Mosaic DIY ECA is a hands-on creative arts club where students explore the ancient craft of mosaic-making. We design and assemble colourful patterns and images using tiles, glass, beads, and recycled materials. We also study the cultural history of mosaics across civilisations, linking art with heritage. Our ECA is a safe, inclusive space for experimentation, self-expression, and mindful making.

name: Move Lab
description: MOVE Lab is a student-led club focused on sports science, training, and physical performance. The club aims to make scientific knowledge about exercise and the human body accessible and useful to students of all experience levels, from complete beginners to regular athletes. Sessions will focus on explaining the reasoning behind training methods rather than simply giving students routines to follow.

name: MusicMath
description: We are a unique club: we "hear" mathematics and reinterpret music through a mathematical lens. Explore the connections between advanced math and music theory, run math × music experiments, and discuss where beauty, order, and creativity come from with peers from diverse backgrounds.

name: Musicals Not Operas
description: Musicals not Operas is a passionate, student-led musical theatre community at SCIE, dedicated purely to musical performances and original stage creation. We gather students with genuine enthusiasm and artistic talent for musicals, aiming to build the school’s most outstanding and influential musical club.The club holds weekly rehearsals to refine members’ stage literacy and performance coherence. Our key annual project is the 2027 March Musical Gala, which strings diverse classic musical excerpts into one cohesive stage show. Our club has proven strong independent production capability. We have successfully staged a complete 45-minute original musical entirely run by students, including self-composed music, original lyrics, full costume and makeup design, and independent on-stage performance, marking our mature artistic execution ability.

name: National History Day
description: The National History ECA will focus on preparing the students for the National History Day competition which is usually held in March at Concordia International School Shanghai. In preparation, students will conduct their own research and create a website on the Historical theme of 'Innovation in History: Impact, Influence, Change.' Students will then present their research to a panel of judges on the day of the competition. Winners of the initial competition will have the opportunity to display their projects in the finals in the United States! The ECA will provide an introduction to the NHD competition, and ongoing support for your project

name: Nature History Club
description: The Nature History Club is an ECA in the Natural Science category. Students interested in biological science and the history of science meet up once a week to explore topics beyond the textbook’s level in depth. Usually, the ECA leaders give lectures to the students around a certain biology-related area (e.g., Applied Evolution) and the history of science, while animated videos and fun questions are included to make the lecture more intriguing. There will sometimes be extra activities such as biological experiments taken into practice occasionally during the ECA’s activity time. The Nature History Club is also involved in constructing the SCIE Garden and Greenhouse. We spend a couple of ECA sessions per semester to work on the SCIE Greenhouse, aiming to study plants habitats, investigate plant growing techniques, and plant seeds by ourselves in the SCIE Greenhouse. Our efforts on the greenhouse will be recorded in our greenhouse journals, which might be published in the future. The Nature History Club encourages students to voice out their own thoughts and be the lecturer. We will spare several lessons for these lecturer students.

name: NeighborLink
description: NeighborLink acts as a bridge connecting SCIE students and Volunteer Shenzhen. We curate suitable student volunteer projects, offer clear registration guidance, and build team platforms for participants to join community service together. Members gain official, verifiable volunteer service records. This ECA helps students step outside campus, develop empathy, communication and problem-solving skills, while contributing youth energy to local communities.

name: Nice Calculus
description: "Nice Calculus" is the newly rebranded continuation of our previous "Calculus" ECA. Derived from the names of its co-leaders, Niko and Bruce, the name "Nice" reflects our club's core educational philosophy. This year, we go beyond teaching rigorous calculus concepts and advanced techniques; our primary focus is helping students develop a profound mathematical intuition—a crucial skill often overlooked in traditional high school curriculums. We will achieve this through a highly visual teaching style, utilizing custom-programmed mathematics animations (such as those built with Python's Manim) and interactive visualization applications. By stepping away from purely algebraic problem-solving, we aim to demonstrate that sensing math geometrically, physically, and visually strengthens independent thinking and fundamentally transforms how students understand the nature of mathematics. Furthermore, based on feedback from previous terms, we have significantly upgraded our syllabus. We are extending our lessons to include applied mathematics topics, such as the multivariable calculus essential for higher-level physics and engineering. By pairing these advanced concepts with concrete examples and visual tools, we ensure our members gain a comprehensive, well-rounded mastery of mathematics.

name: Nirvana
description: We are a flag football team that have been competed in an international school league for years.

name: OC Idea Hub
description: This ECA is a creative community for students passionate about original characters (OC) design, visual world-building and imaginative expression.
