Our members will be able to explore how to visualise fictional personas, design their original characters(such as costume designing and story plotting), and present them by hand-drawing. Apart from personal creative development, our group wants to create a society which encourages the members to visualize, improve and share their idea. This community offers some guidelines for building up original worlds and characters, and provides a platform to make us brainstorm together and share our thoughts.

name: Olympiad in Informatics (OI)
description: Olympiad in Informatics is a competitive programming activity of algorithms and discrete mathematics. Club members solve selected, inspiring problems together on online judge platforms (e.g. Codeforces, Luogu); specific problems are chosen to best reveal how intriguing the subject is. The club also focuses on highlighting the fascinating intersection between mathematics and computer science, for example how computers could aid counting problems and logic verification. Above all, our primary goal is to share how engaging and fun competitive programming can be, gathering more people to join. We will also organize students to participate in online/offline competitive programming contests in allocated teams.

name: Paper Airplane Technology Institution (PATI)
description: Our club Paper Airplane Technology Institute (will be called as ‘PATI’ in the following) is a club that is aimed to teach and support our members to learn, make and fly their paper airplane made by themselves. We try to combine aviation principles, physics and handcrafting as interests into the events of our club in the following semester.

name: Paper Quilling Club
description: This Paper Quilling ECA is a creative art community dedicated to the traditional craft of paper quilling — the art of rolling, shaping and gluing thin paper strips to form delicate decorative artworks. We welcome students of all skill levels, from complete beginners to those with prior crafting experience. In our sessions, members will master fundamental quilling techniques and create a wide range of works, including bookmarks, greeting cards, wall art and 3D miniatures. Beyond hands-on creation, the club integrates creative expression, aesthetic appreciation and public welfare. We will organise themed creation projects and donate selected works to community charity programs. Our club aims to provide a relaxing, supportive space for students to unwind from academic pressure, nurture patience and fine motor skills, and connect with peers who share a passion for handmade art.

name: Pause.
description: ‘Pause.’ is a community designed to make mindfulness practical, accessible, and relevant to everyday student life. Rather than treating mindfulness as simply “sitting still and meditating,” the club explores how attention, awareness, and intentional reflection can influence the way we study, communicate, manage stress, and experience everyday moments. Each session combines a short guided mindfulness practice with an interactive activity or discussion. Students may explore breathing and grounding exercises, mindful movement, attention training, gratitude, mindful listening, digital awareness, and reflection. No previous experience is required, and students are encouraged to participate at their own comfort level. The goal is not to eliminate stress or constantly “feel positive,” but to develop the ability to notice our thoughts, emotions, and surroundings without immediately reacting to them. Through regular practice, Pause. aims to help students become more attentive to themselves and the people around them.

name: Philomath
description: Philomath ECA is provided for those that are interested to mathematics, and want to thrive deeper into it! We will start the first semester by introducing Group Theory, which is one of the most fundamental concepts in mathematics when stepping into university. The full outline of the ECA is similar to Cambridge’s style of teaching group theory, which is believed to be the most effective amongst all. Overall, this ECA can increase student’s ability in mathematics, which helps application by adding more extra-curriculum knowledge.

name: Philosophy of religions
description: Philosophy of Religions introduces students to different religions, exploring their origins, beliefs, texts, traditions, history and influence on society and culture. The ECA aims to provide an open and non-religious environment where students can learn about different perspectives and discuss questions surrounding religion.

name: Physics Frontier
description: Our club is mainly lecture-based, and I, as the leader of the club, will conduct most of these lectures. These lectures aim to provide a revision and a prevision of school contents for club members, and they will cover curriculums from A level, IGCSE, AP physics up to physics competitions like BPHO and Physics Bowl. Every lecture will be around 50 minutes and there are no after school assignments, so the learning atmosphere is quite relaxing.

name: Physics and Philosophy
description: Physics and Philosophy ECA is a student-led interdisciplinary club exploring the conceptual foundations behind scientific theories and their implications for humanity. While physics provides models to describe the universe, philosophy helps us examine the assumptions, interpretations, and consequences behind those models. The club will explore topics including the interpretation of quantum mechanics (such as the measurement problem and Schrödinger’s Cat), the nature of space and time in Einstein’s relativity, the philosophical foundations of scientific methods, and ethical questions arising from technologies such as artificial intelligence and genetic engineering. Activities will include guided discussions, student presentations, thought experiments, debates, and analysis of scientific papers or philosophical texts. Members will be encouraged to move beyond memorising theories and instead ask deeper questions: Why do scientific models work? What does it mean for a theory to represent reality? How should society respond to new technologies? The ECA welcomes students interested in physics, philosophy, mathematics, humanities, or simply exploring challenging ideas through logical reasoning and open discussion.

name: Pickleball Club
description: Pickleball Club is an ECA run by students. The aim of this club is to introduce students to pickleball and create a fun and inclusive atmosphere for students to exercise, learn, and interact with people. With regular training sessions and friendly matches being conducted, members get a chance to practice the basics of the game, improve their techniques, and work together. The club is open to every student irrespective of whether he/she has a background in the game. Apart from practicing sports, the club intends to promote an active and healthy way of life and create a friendly community. We also hope to organize or participate in competitions with other clubs or communities to encourage students to use their skills in real matches.

name: Pitch Observatory
category: SOCIAL Social sports and physical recreation
description: Football is far more than a sport—it is a magnifying glass for history, politics, social class, migration, and identity. From El Clásico in Spain to the Superclásico in Argentina, from the Milan Derby to the North West Derby in England, every classic rivalry carries within it decades or even centuries of cultural tension and collective memory. Our ECA is dedicated to unearthing these stories. The Football Culture Studies Club is a student-led organization that aims to go beyond scores and highlights, delving deeply into the historical roots, social conflicts, and fan cultures behind the world's famous derbies. Through weekly topic sharing, guided discussions, and member-led research projects, we seek to understand: why does football mean so much to people across the globe?

name: Policy Insight
description: The Policy Insight ECA will focus on the subject of public policy. We invite students who are interested in policy, sociology, economics, or just want to dive into the policy around us. Each week, we will select one concrete, relevant case study close to our daily lives, ranging from our school to our community, and even to the whole society, focusing on policy or creating potential policy that might be helpful. We may have opportunities to implement policies. Students will not only learn the theory but also analyze or debate the policy. In this club, anyone who is interested in policy can be the lecturer, raise their doubts, and invite peers to discuss. Our final goal is to turn our daily observations and knowledge into practical outcomes, giving members a platform to contribute to their surroundings.

name: Polyverse
description: Polyverse is a 3D modelling and rendering club where students are able to explore computer graphics mainly through the app Blender. The members will learn the skills of 3D modelling, texturing, lighting, and rendering by developing through hands on practice. The club aims to provide a creative space where students are able to turn ideas into digital works, such as designing characters and environments to create complete animations. They will collaborate on group projects, share techniques, and explore art and technology. No prior experience is required, and everyone is welcome to learn, create, and experiment.

name: Psychology Union
description: Psychology Union is a proposed ECA open to all SCIE students. It will tentatively be held every Monday as a weekly lecture-based activity. The main aim is to bring together psychology-related clubs at SCIE and create a shared platform for students who are interested in psychology. Instead of functioning as one single club, Psychology Union will work more like a network. Students can attend weekly lectures to gain a general understanding of psychology, and they can also join different club projects based on their own interests.

name: Psyminar
description: Against the widespread student psychological pressure, this ECA aims to improve students’ health and well-being by targeting the gut-mental health link. Scientific research identifies the gut as the human “second brain”, and imbalanced gut microbiota or impaired gut barrier function can significantly raise stress hormone levels and contribute to anxiety and low mood. Regarding the link between intestinal health and mental wellbeing, this ECA translates science into accessible activities. The ECA aims to raise awareness of nutrition mental health connections via practical exercises and self tracking, thus improving mental wellbeing. In summary, this ECA combines biological knowledge, neuroscience, and psychology with lifestyle management to achieve mental wellbeing via dietary approaches.

name: Public Philisophy
description: The Public Philosophy Club is a space where students come together to explore ideas that matter. Whether we’re discussing ethics, identity, the nature of reality, or how philosophy can inform public life, this is the platform to think deeply and share openly.

name: Public-Risk Analysis Club
description: We are a student-led research collective dedicated to dissecting aviation disasters through the lens of public safety. Every session, we reconstruct one historic crash—from cockpit voice recordings to wreckage distribution—and apply the Swiss Cheese Model to trace how minor errors align into catastrophic outcomes. Beyond storytelling, we build our own database: mapping accident hotspots, analyzing pilot age-to-experience correlation (the “U‑curve” of risk), and studying human factors like crew familiarity and circadian rhythms. Our mission is not morbid curiosity, but rational vigilance—transforming tragedy into actionable safety intelligence. We believe every black box holds a lesson not just for aviation, but for emergency response, risk communication, and everyday decision-making. If you seek truth in data and respect in remembrance, join us in rewriting the odds—because the safest flight is the one we never stop learning from.

name: Quicksilver
description: Quicksilver studio has not only been a music club, but the heart of SCIE’s musical expression. As one of the most representative music clubs, we aim for every music lover to find a place to express and showcase, to meet someone with the same hobby, to encounter new and fun people from different ages and backgrounds, or to simply find a place to enjoy music and harmony. Quicksilver is a community built on mutual respect, friendship, and a shared, burning passion for music. We are "equal friends" where every voice is heard, and every unique style is encouraged. Our goal is to create a safe, supportive, and inspiring environment where members can be their authentic selves, shine in their own way, and, most importantly, play the “coolest music” with reliable people. We meet to share music, sing songs, and perform our souls out.

name: RIOT RUNNER
description: RIOT RUNNERS (henceforth RR) is a running team that welcomes runners at all levels.

name: ReaL People
description: ReaL People is a student-led game-development community that has been running for two years. During this time, members have worked together to turn ideas into playable experiences through writing, art, design, programming, audio, translation, testing, and production planning. Our major project, Preface, is an original narrative game developed collaboratively through shared work on worldbuilding, branching dialogue, interactive design, character and environment concepts, models, bilingual text, and playtesting. Our club records document this process across pages for story structure, interaction lists, character development, dialogue, translation, and visual assets. This year, we will continue as a practical creative studio where students learn through small team projects, structured feedback, and iterative improvement.

name: Red Cross
description: SCIE Red Cross, founded in 2010, is one of the oldest and largest societies in Shenzhen College of International Education. It is an outstanding social ECA certified by international organizations, dedicated to promoting humanitarian spirit of borderless care. Under the guidance of Shenzhen Red Cross headquarters and school medical teachers, we integrate first aid training, charity volunteer activities and mental health promotion. We hold regular after-school activities every Tuesday, providing systematic first aid knowledge learning, forming first aid teams for school sports events, carrying out volunteer services at Min'ai Welfare Institute, organizing AHA first aid certificate training, Mental Health Week and first aid lectures. We also launch new projects including first aid handbook compilation and off-campus community first aid teaching, committed to serving the campus and the public with practical humanitarian actions.

name: Relevé Balllet Ensemble
description: Relevé Ballet Ensemble is a student-led dance ECA designed for students who love ballet and seek opportunities to dance on the stage. The ECA provides opportunities for students to develop ballet techniques and artistic expression in a supportive and collaborative environment. Through regular activities, members will be introduced to ballet works from different choreographers, styles, and historical periods, developing a broader understanding of this art form. In addition, we will explore choreography and performance, allowing members to work together to create dance pieces and perform at events like SCIE Got Talent and New Year Concert.

name: Resonance: The Music & Ideology Club
description: Resonance is a discussion-based ECA dedicated to exploring the deeper ideologies, political messages, and social representations embedded within popular and alternative music. Far from just listening to catchy tunes, we analyze music as a historical and cultural artifact. We will dissect how artists use their platforms to express the struggles of specific demographics, challenge the status quo, and reflect the historical zeitgeist of their eras. For example, we will analyze Green Day's American Idiot as a critique of post-9/11 media paranoia, exploring who the "idiot" represents and what generational anxieties the album voices. By bridging music with social sciences and history, members will develop critical media literacy, learn to interpret complex narratives, and enjoy lively, respectful debates about the soundtracks that shape our society.

name: Running for Athletic Performance
description: A mix of running styles that aim to improve athletic perfomance in sports. The aim is to diversify the types of running including sprinting to slow jogging in order to improve fitness in a way that's engaging and that can provide tangible effects. This is not simply just running for an hour, it's structured and motivational.

name: SCIE Anatomy Club
description: The Anatomy Club aims to provide students with a deeper understanding of human anatomy and biological structures through both theoretical learning and hands-on practical activities. Members will explore topics such as the nervous system, respiratory system, circulatory system and other human organs/ systems. The club also conducts practical sessions using animal specimens, including frogs and pig organs such as the kidney, lung, and brain, to help members connect anatomical knowledge with real biological structures. This year, we also hope to introduce basic suturing practice to expand members’ understanding of practical medical techniques.

name: SCIE Basketball League
description: This is a formal 5v5 basketball tournament in SCIE. There are 5 teams in this ECA lead by various captains-all are from SISAC school team or ISL school team-to compete for the final championship in the end of this school year. There will be a tryount monitored by coaches from SISAC and ISL team to ensure the impartiality of picking the players. Every basketball enthusiasts can attend this ECA. The players are drafted by five teams' captains to form a team that at least contain 8 team members. The rountine in the ECA are divided into two parts-regular season and the playoffs season. Firstly, the five teams are playing against each other during the regular season to get the four playoffs spot, meaning that one team will not be in the playoffs competitions. Then, the games in playoffs will be one-off games, which makes winning more coincidential and ensures the tournament will end before the march(won't affect by the external examination schedule).

name: SCIE Biologue
description: This eca aims to report recent events in the campus and explain them in a biological and scientific way, and to present it to the students every two weeks as a magazine.

name: SCIE Champion League
description: The SCIE Champion League (SCL) is an inclusive, intramural 6-a-side football league dedicated to fostering sportsmanship, teamwork, and healthy competition within the school community. Designed to welcome students of all genders and skill levels—from absolute beginners to advanced players—SCL prioritizes passion and creativity over technical perfection, providing a highly supportive environment for athletic expression. A defining feature of the league is its NBA-inspired draft mechanism. At the beginning of the academic year, all participants undergo a skills assessment followed by a structured draft, ensuring balanced team rosters and highly competitive midday matches. Beyond intramural play, SCL also unites its top talents into a representative squad to compete in friendly matches against other international schools. More than just a sports tournament, SCL acts as a dynamic campus platform that bridges diverse student groups, cultivates school spirit, and promotes holistic development through a shared love of the beautiful game.

name: SCIE Cycling Team (SCT)
description: SCT is a cycling club that aims to help students ride safely, correctly and confidently while enjoying the sport of cycling. We welcome riders of different experience levels and provide guidance on cycling skills, road safety, group riding and basic bike maintenance. We also introduce sports science knowledge, including endurance training, pacing, recovery and fitness management, so members can improve their performance in a healthy and sustainable way. Through regular training and group rides, SCT hopes to promote fitness, teamwork and a long-term interest in cycling.

name: SCIE Dub Club
description: The SCIE Dub Club (SDC) offers students an engaging platform to explore the art of voice acting and dubbing. Through weekly sessions, members practice dubbing selected scenes from animations, movies, and TV series in a relaxed and supportive environment. The club focuses on developing vocal flexibility, emotional expression, and technical skills—including voice modulation for different character types . Members also learn about script adaptation, audio synchronization, and basic sound editing. SDC encourages collaboration and creativity, allowing students to perform individually or in groups, share feedback, and improve together. Whether for fun, skill-building, or connecting with like-minded peers, the club aims to cultivate confidence, linguistic ability, and an appreciation for performance arts. No prior experience is required—only enthusiasm for storytelling through voice.

name: SCIE Economics Hub
description: SCIE Economics Hub is an economics society that introduces students to the subject and guides those preparing to study economics at the university level. We focus on developing an intuitive understanding of the conceptual frameworks central to modern economic theory. We use mathematical modeling where helpful to illustrate key economic methods and formal definitions. We welcome all students interested in economics to join us, explore the subject, and share ideas with a cohort of passionate and intellectually curious peers.

name: SCIE Fashion Show
description: Fashion Show is a student-led ECA where members work together to organize the annual school Fashion Show. Members will be divided into different departments and take part in different parts of the preparation, such as deciding the theme, organizing auditions, publicity, model and designer management, and planning the final show. Throughout the process, members are encouraged to share their own ideas and take responsibility for different tasks. Although our final goal is to organize the Fashion Show, the ECA is also a place for students who are interested in fashion, design, media, event planning, or simply want to be part of a creative project and work with other students.

name: SCIE Fencing team
description: Our club brings fencing to campus through engaging activities with a strong emphasis on actual bouting. We organize practice matches and friendly competitions, helping members learn by doing. Everyone can find a suitable sparring partner and gain valuable experience through live fencing. Our goal is to create a vibrant community where students enjoy the thrill of real combat while developing their skills in a safe and encouraging atmosphere.

name: SCIE Finance Club
description: As one of SCIE's largest and oldest finance clubs (over 10 years of history), SCIE Finance Club (SFC) offers something for everyone—it is built for the ones who are passionate about finance and investing, or simply aiming for a prosperous future. The finance lectures we offered are guaranteed to broaden students’ horizons and give them valuable insights students won't find elsewhere. Our lecture content includes but not limited to compound interest, risk-return tradeoff, candlestick and even behavioral finance. More importantly, the core numbers will lead group discussions about the breaking financial news updated frequently, to help students understand how the financial markets work.

name: SCIE Fitness Club
description: Fitness ECA aims to help students develop a scientific, safe, and sustainable approach to resistance training and physical fitness. Rather than simply exercising together, members will learn the principles behind effective training, including exercise technique, movement mechanics, training progression, recovery, and basic program design. As the ECA leader, I have 3 years of self-weight training and 2 years of systematic resistance-training experience and have developed a deeper understanding of exercise selection, movement patterns, training volume and intensity, fatigue management, and the logic behind different training approaches. I hope to share these ideas in an accessible and practical way, helping members understand not only how to perform an exercise, but also why it is performed in a certain way. Sessions will combine short explanations, practical demonstrations, movement workshops, form analysis, and discussion. The ECA will be suitable for both beginners who want to start training safely and more experienced students who want to improve their understanding of training.

name: SCIE Golf Society
description: founded 2 years ago, the SCIE Golf Society is a fantastic ECA for golfers to practice, communicate and improve. This year, we'll be focusing on playing tournaments and helping the school to form its varsity to participate in inter-school competitions.

name: SCIE Guitar Club
description: SCIE Guitar Club is a student‑led hobby‑oriented community open to all students, regardless of prior guitar experience. We welcome absolute beginners who have never touched an instrument, as well as intermediate and advanced guitar players. Our club creates a relaxed, supportive space for students to share passion for string‑instrument music. Members can practice acoustic or electric guitar, exchange playing tips, learn popular songs, and jam with peers. We encourage mutual help: experienced players will share basic techniques for new members. We aim to build a friendly musical community where students can unwind from academic pressure and connect with others who love guitar music.

name: SCIE HMA
description: Our club prioritizes safety while fostering competitiveness, creating an academic and practical growth platform for cold weapon and martial art. All techniques we learn are from official textbooks of martial arts.

name: SCIE Historical Committee
description: History ECA that tutors students from G1-G2 about IGCSE content. But also adds additional content to whatever the students are interested in.

name: SCIE Ink & Quills Literary Magazine
description: SCIE Ink & Quills Literature Magazine 2026–27 Recruitment Ink & Quills consists of two parts: ✦ Creative Writing Sessions: Weekly Club Activities Fiction · Creative Nonfiction · Poetry Lessons ✦ Magazine Publication Submissions · Editing · Proofreading · Typesetting · Design · Printing We welcome everyone: Writers / Columnists Content Editors Formatting Editors Designers Photographers / Artists If you enjoy writing, editing, or design—or if you’d like to be hands-on in the entire process of creating a campus literary magazine, from first draft to print—we invite you to join Ink & Quills!

name: SCIE Linguistics Club
description: The Linguistics Club is a student-led club that explores how language works and how it shapes our understanding of society. Through interactive quizzes, discussions, presentations, and activities, we explore topics including sociolinguistics, language and gender, semantics, phonetics, and language diversity. The club aims to make linguistics accessible and engaging while encouraging students to question assumptions about language and discover how it connects to everyday life.

name: SCIE Mahjong League
description: We consider Mahjong as an excellent mind sport. As so, we provide opportunity for student to attend in our monthly competitions, where students can attend freely everyday and cumulate scores. For beginners, we provide lessons of Mahjong of basic rules to techniques both in regular games and specific strategy in tournament, where students will come up to teach others based on professional books. This is also a place for students to meet other people who have similar interests, where we can have fun and reduce stress from studying. In addition, this can also express and intrigue people's interests of traditional cultures.

name: SCIE Media
description: SCIE Media aims to create a student-led media platform that documents school life, shares student voices, and strengthens the connection within the SCIE community and to the public. Members will conduct interviews, produce short videos, and manage social media content to showcase campus events, student experiences, and school culture.

name: SCIE Mock Trial
description: SCIE Mock trial will train students to become skilled attorneys and witnesses, prepared to participate in high level mock trial competitions such as International Mock Trial, Peer Potential Mock Trial, etc. Through teaching the federal rules of evidence, procedures of a trial, public speaking skills, performance tips, students will be prepared for success in mock trial while also getting an introduction to law related knowledge.

name: SCIE Philosophy Club
description: SCIE Philosophy Club is a discussion-based ECA for students interested in examining everyday questions more carefully. Each session begins with a question, thought experiment, short reading, film clip, or real-world case, followed by student-led discussion and argument. Topics may include free will, personal identity, morality, knowledge, language, aesthetics, political philosophy, and questions raised by new technologies such as artificial intelligence. Rather than requiring previous knowledge of philosophy, the club will introduce philosophical ideas when they become useful for understanding the question at hand. Members will learn to identify assumptions, construct arguments, respond to objections, and revise their views through discussion. We hope to create an open environment in which disagreement is treated as something to investigate rather than something that has to be resolved immediately.

name: SCIE Puzzle Hunter
description: Puzzle Hunt is an event where teams compete to solve a series of puzzles. It originated from MIT in 1981 and has now become one of the most popular events in universities. Puzzle Hunt is a community with diversity. Everyone can find their excellent field. In SCIE Puzzle Hunter, students will delve into different types of puzzles: logic puzzles, crosswords, cryptography, steganography, detective fiction, linguistics, etc. Through this process, we will explore useful techniques that can be used in puzzle hunt: searching, frequency analysis, brute force machines, solvers, etc. We will try past puzzle hunts like MIT Mystery Hunt and Microsoft Puzzle Hunt to feel the charm of those exciting puzzle structures and designs. Furthermore, we will form teams to participate in those ongoing hunts and compete with teams from all over the world. Like those hunts held by other universities, our ultimate goal is to write our own SCIE Puzzle Hunt in this year.

name: SCIE ROWING
description: SCIE Rowing is a club founded in 2021, we believe that Rowing is not only a sport that improves personal performance, but also a test of perseverance and teamwork ability. Rowing is also highly respected in prestigious schools in Britain and the United States, and most schools have their ownrowing teams. For students who yearn for Oxford and Cambridge, rowing is even more an elitesport with a centuries-old cultural heritage, because the most famous sports event between the two universities is the Oxford-Cambridge Boat Race.

name: SCIE RhythmGames
description: The SCIE Rhythm Games ECA targets players interested in further understanding rhythm games and making friends with similar interests. The ECA focuses on building strong connections between players and educating players on rhythm game chart production. During each session, a designated presenter will provide a short introduction lasting 15 to 30 minutes around a typical type of rhythm game, famous rhythm game music producer, or chart production. Advanced players knowledgeable about the specific topics could volunteer to be the presenter in charge of the introductions for the weeks, which helps improve the quality of content and sense of participation. Members can stay after the introduction to attend activities such as video recording or join multi-player mode with other members. Regular activities such as song producer guessing, draw and guess, and friendly competition amongst club members will also be available. This ECA plans to provide lessons and activities that alternate between different options. The session will last from 4:45 to 5:15. The Game introduction will focus on a famous rhythm game, introducing its mechanism, style of music and art, well-known songs and characters, and strengths and weaknesses. Music producers' introductions will focus on their music groups, how their style and genre changed over time, their best songs, and the famous rhythm game songs they produced. The presenter will present the topic each week with a PowerPoint presentation and short clips of the game and music. Below is a brief draft for the first 10 ECA sessions.

name: SCIE Robotics Team
description: SCIE Robotics Team is SCIE’s student-led FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC) programme, returning for its third year. Each season, members work together to design, build, program and drive a robot for a new competition game released worldwide. FTC combines the energy and teamwork of a sport with real engineering, creativity and strategy. The team will compete in official FTC qualifying tournaments, work towards advancement to championship events. No previous robotics experience is required. New members receive structured training and can explore mechanical design, CAD, electronics, software, computer vision, match strategy, media, business and community outreach. Whether you want to machine a mechanism, write autonomous code, secure a sponsor or present to judges, there is a meaningful role for you. SCIE’s team has won an FTC qualifier, captained a finalist alliance, received second place for the Inspire Award and won the Innovate Award; its 2025–26 robot also reached third in the global TeleOp rankings. Beyond competition, members showcase robotics at school events, visit technology companies, deliver STEM activities for younger students and collaborate with other FIRST teams to expand impactful outreach in China and the wider world. Come build ambitious things, learn from failure, compete and have fun with a supportive team. FIRST Impact Report: https://www.firstinspires.org/hubfs/web/about/report/annual_report_2025.pdf

name: SCIE Singing Club
description: SCIE Singing Club is a place for students who enjoy singing or want to improve their singing skills. The club focuses on teaching basic singing techniques, such as vocal warm-ups, breathing control, pitch, and rhythm. We hope to create a comfortable and supportive environment where everyone can practice singing without feeling nervous or pressured. The club welcomes students of all experience levels, including beginners who may not have much confidence in their voice. Through regular practices and group activities, members can gradually improve their skills and become more comfortable performing in front of others. If possible, we hope to participate in school performances such as SGT, giving members opportunities to share their progress and experience singing on stage.

name: SCIE Swimming Team
description: Swimming Team offers an inclusive platform for both enthusiastic recreational swimmers and competitive skilled athletes. Members improve physical fitness, build stamina and develop water‑safety awareness including basic lifesaving knowledge through regular group training sessions. We value teamwork and collective spirit greatly: teammates support one another during practice, share skills and encourage each other to push personal limits. Participants take part in inter‑school swimming competitions, where they gain real‑world competitive experience, learn to handle pressure and foster sportsmanship. Beyond races, our team creates a welcoming community. Regardless of initial ability, every member gets opportunities to grow, cooperate with peers and build resilience both in and out of the pool.

name: SCIE Table Tennis League
description: STTL is established for gathering all table tennis lover inside the campus, training together for better performance and forming matches within school, we have represent SCIE for friendly matches with SGA and Basis for the past two years.

name: SCIE Touhou Club
description: SCIE Touhou Club will become a creative and cultural hub dedicated to exploring the rich, fan-driven ecosystem of the Touhou Project—one of the world's most iconic indie subcultures, which includes vibrant secondary creations, spanning diverse music remixes, digital art, comics, fanbooks, literature, and game design. This club offers an enviroment for students to appreciate unique soundtracks, analyze East Asian folklore/mythology, and share creative works.

name: SCIE Visual Novel Horizon
description: SCIE Visual Novel Horizon is an interdisciplinary platform dedicated to exploring visual novels as a dynamic medium uniting interactive literature, visual arts, and digital technology. Guided by our motto, "Visual novels, tech, and explorations beyond the horizon," the club examines the thematic and structural depth of visual novels through multi-faceted critical frameworks, drawing insights from literature, philosophy, psychology, sociology, and ethics. In parallel with literary critique, we deconstruct the technical and creative craftsmanship required to build compelling visual novels. Members share insights into game engine programming, branching narrative structures, artistic styling, and adaptive sound design. SCIE Visual Novel Horizon provides an open, intellectually rigorous stage where students can present their analyses, share developmental techniques, and engage in candid peer debate. By embracing differing viewpoints, agreement, and constructive disagreement, the club cultivates both sharp critical thinkers and capable multimedia creators.

name: SCIE Vocaloid Club
description: SCIE Vocaloid Club explores Japanese Vocaloid music and culture through music appreciation, analysis, and discussions on iconic virtual singers, producers, and the evolution of Vocaloid technology. We also explore the development of Vocaloid music culture, providing a welcoming platform for members to share interests, deepen their understanding, and connect with fellow Vocaloid enthusiasts.

name: SCIE badminton club
description: School Badminton Club Our school badminton club is a friendly and energetic place for students who enjoy playing badminton and want to improve their skills. The club welcomes both beginners and experienced players, so everyone has a chance to participate. During weekly training sessions, members practise important skills such as serving, smashing, footwork, and teamwork. Coaches also organise fitness exercises and practice matches to help students become stronger and more confident on the court. Besides regular training, the club takes part in different competitions throughout the school year. Members can compete in singles and doubles matches against with each others. These events encourage students to challenge themselves, learn from their mistakes, and improve their performance. Overall, the badminton club is a great opportunity to stay active, make new friends, develop sporting skills, and enjoy exciting competitions.

name: SCIE debate club
description: SCIE debate club aims to coach students that are passionate about debate. We will bring them to tournaments like ROD

name: SCIE tennis club
description: The SCIE Tennis Club is a student-led sports ECA dedicated to promoting tennis and an active lifestyle within our school community. We welcome players of all skill levels—from beginners learning the basics to advanced players refining their techniques. Weekly training sessions focus on skill development, match practice, and fitness, while friendly intra-club and inter school tournaments provide competitive opportunities throughout the year. Beyond improving tennis abilities, our club cultivates teamwork, discipline, and sportsmanship. We also organize social events and exhibitions to grow the tennis culture on campus. Through regular practice and competition, members build lasting friendships, develop leadership skills, and maintain a healthy balance between academics and physical wellbeing.

name: SCIEscape – "Ideas beyond the syllabus."
description: SCIEscape is a student-led publication platform dedicated to exploring ideas in politics, philosophy, and economics beyond the boundaries of the classroom. Recognizing that many students engage deeply with complex social questions but lack a structured space to share their perspectives, We established a platform where curiosity could become public dialogue. We led a student editorial team in collaboration with history faculty members, organizing a monthly article selection process that encouraged rigorous argument, interdisciplinary thinking, and thoughtful discussion. Contributors explored topics ranging from political institutions and philosophical debates to economic issues shaping contemporary society, transforming individual interests into accessible intellectual conversations. Beyond simply publishing articles, SCIEscape created a community where students learned to refine their ideas, respond to different viewpoints, and communicate arguments to a broader audience. Through this initiative, we aimed to cultivate a culture of inquiry where students could move beyond textbook knowledge, connect academic concepts with real-world issues, and participate actively in shaping intellectual discourse within the school community.

name: SHUTTER STUDIO
description: We are SHUTTER STUDIO, which is a traditional student photography and video ECA established long time ago since 2022-2023. And we are also the first video/photography studio created in SCIE. And we have many achievement in the history, for example, we used to film 2023-2024 SGT semi-final Video, 2023-2024 fashion show video, 2023-2024 world book week video as well. Besides, we are also adept at taking photo, for instance, we used to held many photography booths at Halloween Carnival and also took part in many school activities like SGT, NYC and even Sports Day. And we finally yield many fascinating photos too. Overall, despite we have an extraordinary history in the past, we have to re-start this year due to one year suspension before. However, I think we will still be ambitious, trying our best to capture more photos and cultivate students photography skills and interests this year in the campus. And me, as a new leader of this club, I believe we gonna motivate the development of media and photography in the school this year too.

name: SISAC BOYS VOLLEYBALL
description: ECA for the School Volleyball team

name: SISAC GIRLS VOLLEYBALL
description: ECA for the School Volleyball team

name: SISAC STORM FRISBEE TEAM
description: School Frisbee team

name: Science Education for Girls
description: SEG, Science Education for Girls, started in 2020, is open to all who share a love for exploration. We aim to advocate for female diseases and mental health illnesses. We have been posting essays on multiple social media sources, including WeChat accounts and Red Notes. We are committed to encouraging more girls to emphasize not only the sciences, but also their health. To pursue dreams with support and guidance. This year, we will create a space where female mental illnesses are emphasized, creating an opportunity for members to explore topics from pre-menstrual syndrome to Briquet’s syndrome. Members can enjoy discussions; together, we can make an impact in our society.

name: Science Newsletter Club
description: The Science Newsletter Club (SNC) is an ECA dedicated to promoting scientific knowledge and curiosity within our school community. Through our regular newsletters, we will introduce a wide range of scientific topics, from interesting facts and everyday phenomena to recent discoveries and developments in science. Members will have the opportunity to research scientific topics, develop their scientific communication and writing skills, and collaborate to create informative content for the wider school community. The club aims to encourage students to explore the world of science beyond the classroom and foster curiosity.

name: Science, Technology, and Society (STS) Club
description: The Science, Technology, and Society (STS) Club - "Innovating Today, Transforming Tomorrow" - serves as a dynamic platform for students to explore the intricate relationships between scientific advancements, technological innovations, and their societal impacts. Our mission is to foster critical thinking and interdisciplinary collaboration, empowering students to understand and address contemporary global challenges through the lens of STS. In addition to engaging discussions and research, the club encourages students to form teams and incubate STS-related projects that leverage technology to create positive societal change. These projects may focus on areas such as sustainable development, social equity, ethical technology, and public health. The STS Club aims to cultivate a generation of socially responsible innovators equipped to navigate and shape the future of our interconnected world. Furthermore, the club aspires to publish two issues of an STS journal annually. This initiative will provide students with the opportunity to engage in academic writing, peer review processes, and the publication of original research and essays. By contributing to this journal, members will gain practical experience in scholarly communication and deepen their understanding of the interdisciplinary nature of STS.

name: Scuba Diving Club
description: SCIE Scuba Diving Club is a sports-focused ECA dedicated to promoting scuba diving culture and marine environmental protection. We welcome both PADI-certified divers and ocean-loving students without certification as land volunteers. We run regular sessions on PADI OW foundational theory, diving safety and marine ecosystem knowledge. In summer, we organize certified open-water diving trips to Shenzhen Dapeng, with free equipment including BCD and wetsuits provided. Members can take part in public-welfare dives to clear marine litter, earning community service hours while contributing to ocean conservation. Our club aims to build a community for diving enthusiasts, foster marine protection awareness, and provide safe, well-organized opportunities to explore the underwater world.

name: Sesame Society
description: Our ECA will mostly focus on the cat Sesame, observing its behaviors (e.g health…). More than that, this year we will attempt to introduce stray animals. Our ECA activities are mostly practical based, which we thought it will be more attractive and memorable.

name: Shakespeare's Society
description: At Shakespeare’s Society we aim to help IGCSE and A-level students attain skills to further their creative writing. Creative writing is a crucial part of English language and is most times an overlooked and underperforming part of exams for students. From the structure to the use of imaginative vocabulary, we hope to give a better and more in-depth outline of creative writing, as well as plenty of practice and examples, which will help students reach their full potential of storytelling.

name: She Knew
description: We are a student-led community dedicated to empowering young people to find their voice, build confidence, and think critically about the world around them threw off-campus seminars and open discussions. Our goal is not to give answers, but to create a safe space where teenagers can ask bold questions, challenge stereotypes, and support one another in becoming more thoughtful, independent individuals. We also aim to promote gender equality within campus, creating a safe and welcoming environment for students. We’ll also have an exhibition to showcase our work in the end.

name: Shenzhen International Student Football Fans Club
category: SOCIAL Social sports and physical recreation
description: The Shenzhen International Student Football Fans Club has operated for one academic year and is applying to continue its work. We are a student-led football community that connects SCIE students with local football culture through media, discussion, and supporter activities. During our first year, we produced and published original football content on our WeChat account, including filmed interviews with Shenzhen Juniors Football Club striker Arnold Garita and coach Ramiro Amarelle. These interviews explored players’ professional journeys, training, adapting to football in Shenzhen, and the work behind a local club. We planned questions, conducted interviews, filmed and edited videos, created bilingual subtitles, and shared the final content with students online. This year, we hope to continue documenting Shenzhen football while building a welcoming community for students who enjoy the sport.

name: Silver Impact Initiative
description: Silver Impact Initiative is a student-led club dedicated to improving the lives of older adults through science, community action, and youth leadership. Each month, members explore a real-world challenge affecting older adults, learn from scientific research and experts, and develop practical ideas to address the issue. Not only do we aim to help the elderly, we also reflect upon ourselves after identifying the issues of the elderly to learn how to avoid some preventable issues. Our activities follow a four-step model: Learn → Ideate → Act → Reflect. Students may participate in research, volunteering, community projects, design, or innovation. Members also have opportunities to become Project Leaders, where they develop an idea, form a team, coordinate implementation, and measure the project’s outcomes all with the help of resources of the ECA and its members . Projects remain part of the broader Silver Impact Initiative, allowing future students to build upon previous work and creating continuity beyond individual events. Our initial topics include cancer, Alzheimer’s disease, and hearing loss, with a particular focus on developing a long-term hearing-care initiative for older adults. We aim to connect students with appropriate experts, healthcare institutions, community organizations, and nonprofit or foundation resources where possible.

name: Singularity Nexus
description: Singularity Nexus — where Mathematics, Physics, Algorithms, and Strategy converge. Basic Information: Singularity Nexus is a club dedicated to logical thinking and advanced problem-solving across Mathematics, Physics, Algorithms, and Game Theory. Weekly sessions include teaching core concepts and problem-solving techniques, followed by discussions of challenging problems designed by club leaders. Each year, we create original problems for competitions. Purpose: We bring together students who are passionate about logical thinking and interdisciplinary problem-solving. The club provides a platform for members to exchange ideas, find like-minded peers, and support each other’s learning. Through peer teaching and collaborative discussion, we aim to strengthen SCIE students’ competitiveness and enrich campus life.

name: Skiing Society
description: Skiing Society is a student-run community for skiers and snowboarders of all levels. We are dedicated to creating a supportive, peer-driven environment where members help each other improve, regardless of experience. Every weekend (Saturday or Sunday), the club organises trips to Huafa Indoor Ski Resort in Shenzhen for regular training sessions. Beginners are warmly welcomed—experienced members provide guidance on fundamentals, while more advanced riders share tips on technique and control. Through mutual support and consistent practice, every member can progress safely and confidently. During school holidays, the club also arranges group ski trips to outdoor resorts, offering opportunities to explore real mountains and strengthen friendships beyond campus. Whether you are a complete beginner or an experienced skier, SCIE Ski Club is a place to learn, grow, and share your passion for snow sports. Join us and take your first run with a community that has your back.

name: Social Deduction Board Game Club
description: Social Deduction Board Game Club is a place for students to enjoy strategy-based social games such as Blood on the Clocktower and Werewolf. Members will practise reasoning, communication, persuasion, and teamwork while interacting with different players in a relaxed environment.

name: Society of Chinese Metaphysics
description: this is a society that gathers students who are keen on traditional Chinese metaphysics theory, and the unique philosophy beneath it.

name: Sparkling Dance Club
description: Sparkling is the ideal platform for students who love dancing and aspire to grow as confident performers. Through structured weekly practices and performance preparations, the club helps members refine their dancing skills and gain stage experience at major school events like the SGT, NYC, Halloween, and Fashion Show, immersing themselves in the school’s lively culture. Additionally, the club organizes activities such as random dance sessions during Senior Week, spreading the joy of dance to the wider school community.

name: SpeedCubing
description: The Speedcubing Club is a dynamic and inclusive extracurricular activity dedicated to the art of solving twisty puzzles—most notably the iconic Rubik's Cube—as efficiently as possible. Whether students are complete beginners looking to solve their very first cube or experienced speedcubers aiming to shave seconds off their personal bests, this club provides a supportive and engaging environment for all skill levels. Members will learn foundational solving methods, advanced methods like CFOP (Cross, F2L, OLL, PLL), and optimal finger trick techniques. Beyond just solving puzzles, the club fosters a strong sense of community, encouraging members to share strategies, participate in friendly internal competitions, and celebrate each other's progress. Speedcubing is not just about fast hands; it challenges the mind, builds spatial awareness, and teaches perseverance. Join us to improve your dexterity, challenge your brain, and be part of a vibrant community!

name: Starry Musical
description: Starry Musical aims to provide a platform for discussions between musical lovers and works for the publication of musicals. We welcome every musical lover, or anyone willing to know about musicals. Unlike other musical-related clubs focusing on performing musicals, we mainly create a place for non-singers and non-actors to feel the charm of musicals, which is also a promotion of the thought that “musicals are for everyone as long as you are interested in it”. We will discuss official recordings of musicals, including famous and outstanding foreign ones from Broadway or West End, and more importantly, some Chinese musicals. We want to promote and publicize that there are also good musicals in China, originally produced by Chinese playwrights and Chinese musical actors and actresses. After watching every musical, we plan to showcase our understanding and publicize the musicals by posting videos on social media. Starry Musical channel has already been registered on many platforms online. Everyone in Starry Musical would be responsible for part of the videos, including but not limited to video editing, speakers in the videos and scriptwriters. Also, we plan to link musicals to other topics, like mental illness, depending on the musicals we are watching.

name: Steam & Spark Society
description: The FTC Robotics ECA is a student-led team that designs, builds, and tests a robot for the FIRST Tech Challenge. Members will work together throughout the engineering process, from understanding the competition requirements and developing initial ideas to creating CAD models, manufacturing parts, assembling mechanisms, and testing the completed robot. The ECA will introduce members to practical skills such as CAD, 3D printing, mechanical assembly, tool use, and robot design. Members with different levels of experience are welcome, and more experienced students will help teach and guide newer members. Through hands-on projects, members will learn how individual components work together as part of a complete robotic system. Our main aim is to prepare for the FTC competition while creating a collaborative environment where members can experiment, solve problems, learn from mistakes, and turn their ideas into a working robot.

name: Sustainable Development Initiative
description: Sustainable development initiative has been running for three years. Our hope and mission is to find sustainable ways of living and developing by experimenting in our school and advocate for attention. Our projects include the sustainable garden, which uses zero-chemicals in the growing, and the compost plan, which collaborates with the GC department to make organic compost from kitchen wastes and fallen leaves.

name: TCG Club
description: Provides a place for TCG game competition, communication, and trading.

name: TEDxSCIE
description: TEDxSCIE is the a student-led organisation at SCIE. Since 2017, we have run for 9 years and delivered 8 annual conferences, each bringing together many students and teachers. We turn "Ideas Worth Spreading" into practice by creating an open platform for genuine intellectual exchange. Our weekly workshops cover topic brainstorming, speech writing, verbal delivery, body language, and confidence-building. We also use internal speech competitions to help members improve through practice. The team is divided into four functional departments: Academic, Publicity, Planning, and External Relations. Members get hands-on experience in every stage of organising a large-scale event—from theme selection and speaker outreach to stage execution and on-site coordination. Last academic year, we received the Best Leadership ECA award at SCIE.

name: THE GROVE ——The Student Hideout
description: The Grove is a student-led creative community that aims to create a welcoming space where students can connect, explore new experiences and feel free to be themselves. In a busy school environment, students may sometimes feel stressed, disconnected or unsure where they belong. The Grove provides a supportive environment where students can build meaningful connections through shared experiences and collaborative activities. Rather than focusing on one fixed hobby, The Grove encourages members to explore different interests and create experiences together. Activities may include creative workshops, discussions, film sessions, hands-on projects and other ideas proposed by members. While activities can change, the experience remains the same: connecting with others, creating something together and growing as a community. Most importantly, members are not simply participants. They are encouraged to contribute ideas, take responsibility and gradually lead projects. Through this process, students develop communication, collaboration, organization and leadership skills in an authentic environment. Like a grove formed by many individual trees, The Grove grows through the unique identities and contributions of every member.

name: THE Wotagei M@STERS
description: The club focuses on WotaGei, a dynamic Japanese pop dance born out of the glowsticks moves originally for fans to express the support to the people they like on stages. The dancer usually holds two high-brightness glowsticks, and perform intensely, leaving beautiful trails of light in the air. The study of OtaGei, the varient of WotaGei will also be involved in the club activities. Unlike WotaGei, OtaGei uses no glowsticks, and is typically not considered as stage performances. Instead, it is more of a relax meathod for the dancer to immerse and enjoy the background music. For the estimated 20 years since WotaGei has been founded, numerous enthusiasts have been creating new Wotagei choreography, also known as Waza. There will always be new things to learn and perfect in this unique foreign dance.

name: Tchoukball Club
description: This is Tchoukball ECA, we come together due to the passion for this amazing sport. You may not have even heard of this, but you will learn it in your core PE classes. This is a sport that originated in Switzerland and is now becoming popular in most Asian countries and Regions. This sport is super fun; you won't have any aggressive body contact; instead, all you need to do is work closely with your teammates, act fast, and try your best strategy and angle to attack the net to get points. If you want to make friends with each other and get really interesting experiences, please come to our ECA. Here you can find the best way that teamwork and strategy work with each other. This year, we have two vice presidents: Ethan 24050 and Vitas 25447.

name: Technology, History & Society Forum
description: Our extracurricular activity group is dedicated to creating a safe, open, and comfortable environment where students can freely exchange their unique insights into 3D modeling and explore its practical applications in historical technology, daily life and society. Beyond sharing technical skills, we strive to foster meaningful dialogue among members, encouraging everyone to draw new inspiration and innovative ideas from each other's experiences. We believe learning is a collaborative process, where through active discussion and mutual support, each participant gains valuable knowledge that transcends the software itself. Furthermore, we are committed to translating collective expertise into concrete action. By building a united and collaborative team, we aim to bridge the gap between modeling theory and real-world engineering challenges. Our ultimate goal is to design and implement innovative solutions that meet societal needs—whether it's assistive devices, sustainable design, or community-centered projects. Through this process, we hope to not only enhance our technical skills but also cultivate social responsibility and teamwork, demonstrating that even small-scale creations can have a profound impact on the world around us.

name: Tencent volunteering teaching (TVT)
description: TVT (Tencent Volunteer Teaching) is a platform provided by Tencent Volunteer Organization that connects top-performing students with learners in remote areas through online tutoring. Since launching in 2022, TVT has deeply connected outstanding students from top schools in Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, and even from the UK's G5 universities with students in remote areas who are eager to broaden their horizons and improve their academic performance.

name: The Cloud Watchers
description: The Cloud Watcher is a scientific observation and study group focused on the atmospheric phenomenon. Members learn to identify and classify clouds and optical phenomena (e.g., halos, rainbows), understand their formation principles through atmospheric physics and meteorology, and explore related wider topics such as front, air mass, storm and terrestrial effects. Activities combine outdoor sky observation, data analysis, and group discussion, fostering both scientific inquiry and a deeper connection with the natural environment.

name: The Economics reading club
description: The Economics Reading Club is a student-led enrichment programme designed for our most able and intellectually curious economists, offering a bridge between the A-Level syllabus and the wider world of economic thought. Run by the Economics Department, the club draws on preliminary reading lists recommended by Oxford and Cambridge for Economics applicants, giving students genuine exposure to the kind of texts, arguments, and thinkers they will encounter at university and in admissions interviews.

name: The International Lens
description: The International Lens is for students who see a major news story and think, “I know this matters—but what is actually going on?” Our aim is to make politics, economics, and global affairs easier to understand and much more enjoyable to explore. Each week, we will choose a real event, explain the background in beginner-friendly language, and then do something interactive with it. Members might run a mock election, represent different countries in a crisis, investigate a suspicious headline, compete in a geography challenge, or debate what a government should do next. No previous knowledge is required, and nobody should feel embarrassed about asking a “basic” question. Members will also take turns sharing topics they find interesting and helping one another understand difficult ideas. Last year, we built The International Lens website, which includes beginner lessons, country profiles, event explanations, and a forum. The website will remain a useful resource, but the heart of the ECA will be learning, discussing, questioning, and discovering how surprisingly connected the world is.

name: The Magical Unicorn
description: Stepping into the spotlight to make an audience roar with laughter and bring a fairy-tale world to life! Join us for this term's pantomime, The Magical Unicorn — a tale of adventure, friendship, and a little bit of mischief! Whether you love acting, singing, dancing, designing costumes, marketing, or working behind the scenes with lights and sound, there's a place for you in this production. No experience necessary — just enthusiasm and a willingness to have fun!

name: The Magical Unicorn 1
description: Stepping into the spotlight to make an audience roar with laughter and bring a fairy-tale world to life! Join us for this term's pantomime, The Magical Unicorn — a tale of adventure, friendship, and a little bit of mischief! Whether you love acting, singing, dancing, designing costumes, marketing, or working behind the scenes with lights and sound, there's a place for you in this production. No experience necessary — just enthusiasm and a willingness to have fun!

name: The Pathfinders Collective
description: The Pathfinders Collective is a student-led academic club focused on efficient learning, academic exploration, and college planning. Our goal is to help students understand how to learn efficiently, improve academic performance, and confidently work toward their ideal universities. We invite top‑performing students from various grades to share hands‑on learning strategies and real‑world application insights. Our inclusive peer‑sharing environment encourages members to explore diverse perspectives. By interacting with experienced high‑achievers, we hope that students can acquire efficient study skills to improve academic performance. More than just gaining practical tips, every participant contributes their own thoughts and reflections. We want to foster a mutually beneficial space where everyone learns from one another, grows collectively and makes progress together.

name: The SCIE Snooker and Billiards
description: Our ECA aims to gather the students who are passionate for the pool/snooker/billiards, playing, practicing and communicating. For both beginners and experienced players, they can participate in teach and learn to sharpen the skills. From an alternative perspective, students will exhibit a significant increase in their selection of recreational activities during extracurricular hours, fostering their interests.

name: Theoretical Politics Club
description: Theoretical Politics Club is a discussion-based ECA for students interested in political theory, comparative politics, and the functioning of different political systems. In the first several sessions, members will be introduced to major political theories and concepts, such as liberalism, conservatism, socialism, realism, nationalism, democracy, authoritarianism, legitimacy, state power, and political institutions. After building this theoretical foundation, the club will move toward case-based analysis. Members will examine selected historical and contemporary political regimes, comparing how institutions, ideology, leadership, economic conditions, and social forces shape political outcomes. Sessions will mainly consist of short presentations, guided discussion, debates, and group analysis. The purpose is not to promote any particular political position, but to encourage members to understand political systems from multiple perspectives and develop evidence-based arguments.

name: To-listen倾听屋
description: "To-Listen" is an Extra-Curricular Activity (ECA)/Project Group dedicated to providing online peer counseling and support for teenagers. Our group offers a safe and confidential space where members can engage in meaningful conversations, seek guidance, and receive support from their peers. The core philosophy of "To-Listen" revolves around active listening, empathy, and fostering a supportive community environment.

name: UZIV
description: UZIV has been part of SCIE for 19 years, dedicated to creating positive change through meaningful community service. Our club believes that small acts of kindness can bring lasting impact, and we design activities that connect students with both local needs and wider social concerns. Over the years, we have organised beach cleanups to protect the environment, created art portrait projects to celebrate and encourage children living with challenges, and visited children’s welfare institutions to bring care and companionship. The Charity Bazaar allows us to build a deeper connection with the charity house, as all of our revenue is donated in support of their work. It reflects our belief in collective effort: when many people come together with care and energy, they can create a kinder and more supportive community for everyone. Beyond these regular initiatives, UZIV also serves as a space for creativity and inspiration. We encourage members to design new events and contribute their own ideas, making the club a dynamic platform for student-led action. Every project we take on reflects the diversity of our members’ passions while staying true to our mission of fostering compassion and responsibility.

name: Undergraduate Mathematics Club
description: The University Mathematics Society is a vibrant community for students passionate about the beauty and depth of mathematical thinking. Our activities go beyond the standard curriculum, exploring rigorous topics such as real analysis, linear algebra, number theory, and group theory. We delve into epsilon-delta proofs, eigenvector decompositions, and the subtleties of convergence—building a foundation that turns abstract definitions into powerful tools. Beyond exam preparation, we host guest lectures, problem-solving competitions, and collaborative study groups. Whether you are aiming for Cambridge, Oxford, or simply love a good mathematical challenge, our society offers a welcoming and intellectually stimulating environment. Join us to sharpen your mind, share ideas, and celebrate the elegance of mathematics together. Everyone is welcome—from first-year enthusiasts to final-year experts.

name: University Physics
description: This year, "University Physics" isn't just about memorizing equations—it's about fundamentally changing how we see the universe. We’ll step beyond the standard high school curriculum, moving from the familiar Newtonian world of pushing and pulling forces into the beautifully elegant realm of analytical mechanics. By adopting the Lagrangian approach, we’ll explore the principle of least action, discovering how complex systems can be understood entirely through energy rather than messy vectors. But we won't stop at classical mechanics. We’re also diving into the weird, wonderful frontiers of modern physics. Through concepts like quantum mechanics and special relativity, we’ll unpack mind-bending, counterintuitive ideas that perfectly explain the bizarre realities of our world. At its core, our club is about building genuine physical and mathematical intuition. We want to explore advanced problem-solving methods and theorems you won't find in standard textbooks. By tackling these challenges together, we'll equip you with the strong intuition and deep understanding needed to confidently pursue higher-level physics in the future.

name: Volleyball for fun
description: The ECA is called haikyu volleyball for fun eca. Its purpose is to help students to get in-touched to volleyball or let students practice their volleyball skills. Regular tutorials will be given through the sessions. The aim of this eca is for new students that’s interested in volleyball to actually try and learn new skills and also provide a place for students who already know several skills in volleyball, to practice.

name: We & Horse
description: Our ECA is an Equestrian club called We & Horse. When talking about equestrian, many students simply say it is “horse riding”. However, people neglect that relationship between rider and horses is more significant.before we ride horses, we need to learn how to respect for horses, atthe same time we would receive therapeutic connection from them, so the target of the ECA is letting more people to have not only deeper understanding of equestrian but knowledge of horses, so that helps people to build a healthy relationship with horses and nature.

name: Winglish
description: Our ECA aims to gather students that have interest in teaching younger and/or disabled children. Members can teach any appropriate subject of their interest using English.

name: World Culture Café
description: This ECA is established for students who are interested in different culture. The sessions that this ECA will have will related to Anthropology, Sociology, regional study, cultural study and Philosophy. The topic of this semester will be about eastern Asia’s culture . All the knowledge of the culture is according to books like ‘The Chrysanthemum and Sword’ ‘OTAKU: Japan’s database animal’, ‘From the soil’ and ‘the Individualization of Chinese Society’. We are going to include the transformation of society, the reason why cultures are different, and most importantly, we will have a more objective and more anthropological insight when we are facing cultural differences. The form of the sessions will mainly be teaching with PPT. To make sure the concepts are understandable, there will be many real life examples which are close to daily life. Also, there will be many interactions during the sessions, so that our members can discuss our different ideas.

name: Yarn Club
description: In this club, we will focus on yarn crafts, as the name implies. Members will learn how to crochet, starting with basic techniques such as pulling loops through loops using a hook, and gradually progressing to create intricate items like decorations, dolls, and clothing. We are planning to do more creative work, including exhibitions, collaborations on charitable projects, and crochet workshops for children.

name: Yearbook 2026-2027
description: Yearbook is a student-led ECA dedicated to documenting and celebrating the SCIE community through creative storytelling, photography, design, and collaboration. The ECA works to capture memorable moments from academic events, student activities, sports, ECAs, and everyday campus life, creating a meaningful record of each school year. Members will develop skills in content creation, visual design, communication, project management, and teamwork while contributing to a shared project that represents the diverse voices and experiences of SCIE students. Through collecting stories, designing layouts, and coordinating with different departments and student groups, Yearbook provides students with opportunities to strengthen their creativity and leadership skills while preserving the school’s collective memories.

name: Yoga & Meditation ECA
description: The Yoga and Meditation Club aims to promote physical wellness, mental clarity, and overall well-being. We offer a welcoming space for students to explore yoga and meditation, with weekly sessions focused on yoga asanas (stretching and strength), meditation practices, and sound therapy using various instruments. We also share knowledge on key techniques and terminology to deepen our practice.

name: Youtopia
description: Our ECA is an original economic card game creation society built on a self-designed fictional continent with diverse unique nations. In previous years, our core focus was fusing formal economic academic knowledge with tabletop gameplay, as our team independently designed, balanced and refined a proprietary card game that models real-world market cycles, trade policies and resource allocation. For the upcoming academic year, we pursue dual-track progress: we continue iterating new card expansions and gameplay mechanics, while vastly expanding our lore framework—crafting core protagonists, layered character backstories, inter-nation conflicts and complete narrative arcs to deepen our immersive fantasy world. Additionally, we will launch official social media channels to consistently publish serialized worldbuilding entries, character biographies, game tutorials and behind-the-scenes development content, letting members collectively build a cohesive, self-contained original game IP.

name: ZhaoHui Chinese Orchestra
description: Our ECA brings together students who share a passion for playing traditional Chinese instruments in an ensemble. Based on the solid groundwork of members from previous years, our ECA now consists of wind, string, and percussion sections. By adapting popular music or rehearsing classical pieces, we introduce modern aesthetics that interact with traditional performance practices. During ECA, we practice solo and ensemble repertoire. We cherish our rehearsal time and actively participate in campus competitions, willing to share our appreciation of Chinese traditional music with all schoolmates.

name: Zhuangzi Discussion Club
description: What does it mean to be free? Is success always worth pursuing? How much of our lives should be determined by grades, university offers, competition and other people's expectations? And how can we maintain a sense of balance when the world around us constantly tells us to do more, achieve more and become more? These are not merely philosophical questions. They are questions about everyday life. This ECA explores these questions through the Inner Chapters of the Zhuangzi, one of the most imaginative works of classical Chinese philosophy. Rather than studying Zhuangzi simply as an ancient Chinese thinker, students will encounter his ideas as a provocative conversation partner for the challenges of modern student life. Through stories, paradoxes, thought experiments, close reading and panel discussions, we will explore themes including freedom, perspective, comparison, success, social expectations, identity, uncertainty, change and inner balance. This ECA creates a space where students can step outside the pressure of everyday academic life, question assumptions, encounter different perspectives, and reflect on what they genuinely value. Ultimately, Zhuangzi invites us to consider a deceptively simple question: How can we live freely in a world that constantly tells us who we should be?

name: cinema appreciation
description: This ECA aims to create a space where people in the school feel free to discuss about films with potential strangers in the school face-to-face. The discussions include the individuals' opinions of the themes they recognize, the director intention and how a certain frame gives the audience a certain feeling etc. The basic procedure is the context of the movie then clips of it then discussion.

name: iGEM Club
description: The iGEM Club is a student-led extracurricular activity dedicated to synthetic biology, biotechnology, and interdisciplinary problem-solving. As part of the global iGEM (International Genetically Engineered Machine) competition framework, the club will design, build, and test innovative biological systems to address real-world challenges. Activities include laboratory training, project design, outreach initiatives, and collaborations with international teams. Members will gain experience in scientific research, teamwork, and communication while exploring the ethical and societal dimensions of biotechnology.
